capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: `GET /users/42` produces `transaction: "GET /users/[id]"`, `source: "route"`, `http.route: "/users/[id]"` (Astro's own bracket param syntax, not `:id`). The span is created by the Astro middleware's `instrumentRequestStartHttpServerSpan`, not by @sentry/node's httpIntegration, so it is unaffected by bun's lack of OTel http instrumentation. Same result in both lifecycles; under stream the span envelope carries `sentry.segment.name.source: route`.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent `GET /tagged?t=alpha|beta|gamma` requests, each setting `probe_tag` and capturing an error after a 120ms await: three events with exactly one tag each (alpha/beta/gamma), three distinct trace ids, and each transaction carries only its own tag and the same trace id as its event. The middleware's `withIsolationScope` works on bun.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: `GET /users/77` with `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-1111111111111111-1` plus a baggage header yields a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: 1111111111111111`. `continueTrace` in the Astro middleware handles this, so it does not depend on bun runtime hooks.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:41502/rec')` from inside a handler produces no `http.client` span (the `GET /fetchout` transaction has `spans: []`) and the recorder sees the request with no `sentry-trace` and no `baggage` header. The exact same build run under `node --import ./sentry.server.config.mjs dist/server/entry.mjs` does produce `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41502/rec` and sends both headers, so this is a bun failure, not an Astro one: @sentry/node's NodeFetch integration relies on undici's `undici:request:*` diagnostics channels, which bun's native fetch does not publish.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: No db span on bun in either mysql2 path. Instrumentation path used: the Astro integration's own `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` (Vite build-time channel injection) plus `vite.ssr.noExternal: ['mysql2']` — no Bun build plugin was needed or used, and the injection demonstrably worked (the built chunk contains `tr_ch_apm_tracingChannel("orchestrion:mysql2:query")` wrapping `BaseConnection.query`). With mysql2 3.19.1 (orchestrion range) Sentry subscribes to `orchestrion:mysql2:query` on bun (verified: `start.hasSubscribers = true`) yet the injected wrapper reads `hasSubscribers = false` from its own channel handle and never publishes; the identical dist run on node emits `db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0` as a child span. notes:
Five things a docs page would have to say, none of which any page says today.

1. `@sentry/bundler-plugins` must come from the same build as the rest. Installing the develop tarballs alongside the npm-published `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` makes `npx astro build` die before it does anything: "The requested module '@sentry/core' does not provide an export named 'ServerRuntimeClient'". The published build imports `ServerRuntimeClient` from `@sentry/core`; develop moved it to `@sentry/core/server` (worktree packages/bundler-plugins/build/esm/core/sentry/telemetry.js:2 already uses the new path). Packing it from the worktree fixes it. This is a develop-vs-npm skew, not a bun issue, but it blocks any Astro probe.

2. `bun --preload ./sentry.server.config.mjs` is mandatory, and that is a real gap rather than a bun quirk. The integration injects the server init with `injectScript('page-ssr', ...)`, which lands only in `.astro` page modules — after `astro build`, `grep -rln "Sentry.init" dist/server/chunks/*.mjs` matches exactly one file, the `index.astro` chunk. Astro loads page chunks lazily, so a deployment whose traffic starts on an API route (`src/pages/*.ts`) runs completely uninstrumented until someone renders an `.astro` page: my first run sent zero envelopes for `/boom`, `/users/42` and `/sentinel`, then started working the moment I requested `/`. `--preload` (or `node --import`) closes it, at the cost of the config being evaluated twice, hence the `isInitialized()` guard.

3. Astro's own middleware is what makes this runtime usable at all. Errors, route-parametrised transaction names, isolation and incoming-trace continuation all come from `@sentry/astro/middleware`, which builds the `http.server` span itself when it does not find one. None of them go through @sentry/node's OTel http instrumentation, which is why they survive on bun while everything that *does* depend on runtime hooks (fetch, db) dies.

4. Two independent bun defects sink db spans, and they are worth filing separately.
   - mysql2 >= 3.20.0 (native `mysql2:*` channels): Sentry never subscribes on bun. `Mysql2Integration.setupOnce` calls `waitForTracingChannelBinding`, whose only retry is a single `setTimeout(..., 1)`. On bun that timer fires before the async-context strategy is registered and the code gives up (`fired count: 0`); on node the same timer lands after init (`fired at 188 ms`) and it works. Unref'd timers do fire on bun, so this is an ordering race, not a timer bug — raising the retry count or retrying until the client is ready would fix it.
   - mysql2 < 3.20.0 (orchestrion build-time injection): the Vite plugin injects correctly and Sentry subscribes (`start.hasSubscribers = true` read from a preloaded module in the running app), yet the injected wrapper inside the bundled chunk reads `false` from its own `tracingChannel` handle and skips the publish. I could not reduce this: a minimal `createRequire('diagnostics_channel').tracingChannel(...)` in a dynamically imported chunk (mini/main.mjs) works fine on bun, and identity checks inside the real chunk gave contradictory answers between two patched copies of the same file. The observable fact is solid, though: the identical `dist/` emits `db SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id > 0` under node and nothing under bun.

5. Two smaller things. `vite.ssr.noExternal: ['mysql2']` is required — the Node adapter externalises node_modules by default, and the orchestrion plugin can only transform what Vite bundles; no Bun build plugin was involved. And a connection pool is not enough: mysql2's `lib/base/pool.js:183` calls `conn.query(cmdQuery)` with no trailing callback, and orchestrion's `Callback` wrapper passes such calls through untraced, so the probe uses a module-scope `createConnection` (I did not separately confirm the pool gap on node).

Cosmetic noise seen on bun that is probably worth a look: `Sentry Logger [error]: Failed to read file: native` / `Could not find line 2 in file native`, from ContextLines trying to open bun's synthetic `native:7:39` stack frame, once per captured event.

Astro 7 builds through rolldown-vite; the orchestrion Vite plugin handled it without complaint. Runtime context reported as `"runtime":"node"` — bun is not distinguished, which will make these events hard to find in an issue stream. Environment notes: npm blocked the `esbuild`, `fsevents` and `@sentry/cli` postinstall scripts; esbuild's native binary was present anyway and sourcemap upload was disabled, so neither mattered. Port 41337 was taken by another agent mid-run, hence the switch to 52341. All processes were killed and node_modules removed (242M).

It prescribes exactly the shape I verified: install @sentry/astro + @sentry/cloudflare (:65-79), set "main": "./sentry.server.config.ts" in wrangler.jsonc (:104-113), export `Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({...}), handler)` around `import handler from "@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server"` (:122-145), and register `integrations: [sentry()]` in astro.config.mjs (:160-178). That wiring is correct on develop and it is the only one that works.

Three places where the page is stale, wrong, or silent against develop:
- astro.mdx:12-13 states prerequisites as "Astro 6.0.0 or above" and "@astrojs/cloudflare v13 or above". npm latest is astro 7.3.1 / @astrojs/cloudflare 14.3.0 and the documented setup works unchanged on those, but the floor wording reads stale.
- astro.mdx:21-35 (the "Using Astro 3-5 with @astrojs/cloudflare v12?" expandable) claims "the @sentry/astro integration automatically detects the Cloudflare adapter and wraps your Worker with the @sentry/cloudflare SDK" and tells the reader to skip the custom entry point. On develop with astro 7 / adapter 14 that auto-wrap does not happen at all: with `integrations: [sentry()]` present and only SENTRY_DSN/SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE as wrangler vars, zero envelopes are emitted (control B). The page does scope the claim to Astro 3-5 / adapter v12, which I did not test, but nothing warns that the fallback produces no telemetry rather than an error.
- Nothing anywhere says that `integrations: [sentry()]` is what supplies error capture, parameterized route names and library (db) spans on Cloudflare. It is presented as step 3 of 3 ("Register the Sentry Integration") after the entry point, which reads as optional polish; dropping it leaves a Worker that reports method-only "GET" spans, no db spans, and silently swallows thrown route errors.
notes:
Findings worth carrying forward:

1. Astro on Cloudflare is fully viable on develop and the documented setup is complete and correct. All seven server capabilities pass.

2. The two halves of the setup are BOTH load-bearing and cover different things. `withSentry` in sentry.server.config.ts gives the client, isolation scope, transport, logs and fetch instrumentation. `integrations: [sentry()]` in astro.config.mjs gives error capture (mechanism auto.middleware.astro), parameterized route names / http.route, and build-time channel injection for library spans. Neither substitutes for the other, and dropping the second fails silently and partially (200s and 500s still served, spans still emitted, just degraded and errorless).

3. mysql db spans work on Cloudflare Workers with no Cloudflare-specific Vite plugin at all. The @sentry/astro integration's own Vite plugin already runs @sentry/server-runtime-injection over the server build; `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__.bundler` is present in the emitted dist/server/entry.mjs. A module-scope connection was used, per the Bun K11 guidance, and worked.

4. Build-order trap worth documenting: @astrojs/cloudflare v14 runs @cloudflare/vite-plugin during `astro build`, and that plugin resolves wrangler.jsonc's `main` at config time. Pointing `main` at a dist path (e.g. ./dist/_worker.js/index.js, the shape older Astro-on-Cloudflare guides use) makes `astro build` fail before it can produce that file: "The provided Wrangler config main field (.../dist/_worker.js/index.js) doesn't point to an existing file". The docs' ./sentry.server.config.ts value sidesteps this because the file exists in the source tree, but nothing explains why.

5. `sourceMapsUploadOptions` is now rejected: "[WARN] [@sentry/astro] [Sentry] Removed in v11 and ignored: sourceMapsUploadOptions. Set bundler plugin options directly on the Sentry build options." The Astro guide still documents sourceMapsUploadOptions.

6. Stack frames on captured errors carry no context_line (hasContextLine:false) under wrangler dev even though the build emits sourcemaps. Outside the brief, flagging for whoever looks at Cloudflare source context.

7. Environment friction, for the record: ports 41337, 41998 and 41999 were already held by sibling agents; I moved to 37411 (sink), 37412 (recorder), 37413 (wrangler). npm printed allow-scripts warnings for workerd/esbuild postinstall but the optional platform package workerd-darwin-arm64 was present and wrangler ran fine.

8. Client-side (@sentry/astro browser half, session replay, client route names) was not probed; server runtime only.

9. Cleanup done: wrangler, sink and recorder processes killed by captured pid; app/node_modules removed (probe dir now 4.4M). Rerunning needs the npm install line in `commands` first.

docsNote: No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Astro on Deno. The Astro guide actively says the opposite of what I measured: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/index.mdx:23-27 carries an Alert titled "What runtime do you use?" reading "This SDK currently only works on Node runtimes, such as Node adapter or Vercel with Lambda functions. If you use Cloudflare Workers or Cloudflare Pages, refer to our Astro on Cloudflare guide. Other non-Node runtimes, like Vercel's Edge runtime, are currently not supported." `grep -rni deno` over docs/platforms/javascript/guides/astro/ returns nothing, and `grep -rni astro` over docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/ returns nothing (that guide is only index.mdx + configuration/, with no framework pages at all). So Deno is neither listed as supported nor listed as unsupported; a reader lands on "only Node runtimes" and concludes it will not work, which is wrong for @deno/astro-adapter on Deno 2.9.
notes:
1. Astro runs on Deno without Sentry (checked first, as asked): `@deno/astro-adapter@0.6.0` + astro 7.3.1 built and served `{"id":"42"}` from `/users/42` on Deno 2.9.0. The only build noise is three benign rolldown warnings from the adapter itself, e.g. "[IMPORT_IS_UNDEFINED] Import `start` will always be undefined because there is no matching export in '\0virtual:@deno/astro-adapter:config'" at node_modules/@deno/astro-adapter/src/server.ts:87 — the adapter still honours `deno({ port, hostname })`.

2. BIGGEST GAP, and it is Astro-side, not Deno-side: `@sentry/astro` injects the server init with `injectScript('page-ssr', ...)`, and Astro only applies `page-ssr` to `.astro` page components, not to `.ts`/`.js` endpoint routes. In a first run with no `src/middleware.ts` I hit `/boom` cold: the process printed zero "Sentry Logger" lines, the sink stayed empty, and only after I hit the one `.astro` page did init run. Verified in the build output: dist/server/chunks/index_CDQcGmve.mjs (from index.astro) contains `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/astro"` + the init, while dist/server/chunks/boom_DBViSP1b.mjs (from boom.ts) contains no Sentry import. An API-only Astro app on any adapter therefore silently reports nothing until an `.astro` page is rendered. My workaround — a project `src/middleware.ts` whose first statement imports `sentry.server.config.js` — makes init deterministic, because Astro loads the whole middleware sequence module graph before running any handler; the Sentry middleware is registered `order: 'pre'` and still wraps everything. A docs page for Astro-on-Deno would have to show this, since Deno has no equivalent of the Node `--import @sentry/astro/import` preload (`@sentry/astro/import` is just `import '@sentry/server-runtime-injection/import-hook'`, a Node loader hook).

3. `@sentry/node` under Deno's node compat is in far better shape than the docs imply. It installs every integration, logs "Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks()" (Deno 2.9 has that API), and takes the "Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly" path for every library instrumentation. The Deno import hook from `@sentry/deno` is not involved anywhere.

4. db spans did NOT need any extra wiring. `@sentry/astro` adds `sentryOrchestrionPlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation })` to the Vite config for every non-Cloudflare adapter, Astro's SSR build bundles mysql2 into the page chunk, and the emitted chunk carries the orchestrion channel publishes (188 `orchestrion:*` / `tracingChannel` hits in dist/server/chunks/db_*.mjs). So the answer to "which instrumentation path" is: the Vite build-time orchestrion plugin, applied automatically; no Bun plugin, no Deno import hook, no Cloudflare Vite plugin.

5. Deno K2 reproduces unchanged under Astro: global `fetch` gets neither an `http.client` span nor propagation headers. `node:http` gets both. That is the one capability that is broken here, and it is a runtime gap, not an Astro gap.

6. Cosmetic but user-visible: ContextLines repeatedly errors on Deno-internal stack frames — "Failed to read file: ext:core/01_core.js. Error: Error: ENOENT ..." and "Could not find line 475 in file ext:core/01_core.js" — printed for every captured error when `debug: true`. Events still carry correct context lines for app frames (`hasContextLine: true`).

7. I set `enabled: { client: false }` to keep the probe server-only; the client SDK path was not exercised, so "client errors" is not reported.

8. Housekeeping: both processes (deno app on 41337, sink on 44551) were killed; `node_modules` (242 MB) removed, leaving 1.7 MB of source, dist and logs. Nothing outside $REPRO/cells/M-astro-deno was touched. Only develop tarballs (10.67.0) were installed; 10.73.0 was never fetched.

notes:
Elysia on bun is the smoothest of the non-Node runtime combinations probed: no adapter, no preload flag, no bundler, and every core capability except db-driver breadth works out of the box with the docs' own snippet.

Two SDK bugs found by reading `packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts` and confirmed at runtime:

1. `sdk.name` is `sentry.javascript.bun`, never `sentry.javascript.elysia`. `const options = { ...userOptions, platform, runtime, serverName }` is built BEFORE `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'elysia', ['elysia', options.runtime.name])`, so the elysia metadata is written to `userOptions` and dropped; `initNode(options)` then stamps the Bun metadata. Fix is to call `applySdkMetadata(options, ...)`. This also means the docs' `sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia` front-matter never matches what Sentry receives.

2. `getDefaultIntegrations` in the same file filters `getBunDefaultIntegrations(options)` by `bunServerIntegration().name` (= `'BunServer'`) to drop "Bun's competing root span". The Bun default set on develop no longer contains `BunServer`; it contains `BunHttpServer` (`bunHttpServerIntegration`), so the filter removes nothing and `BunHttpServer` stays in the list (observed in the integration dump). Harmless in practice here because `bunHttpServerIntegration` patches `node:http.Server.prototype.emit`, not `Bun.serve`, and Elysia on Bun uses `Bun.serve` — no duplicate root span was ever observed. Still a dead filter whose stated purpose is unmet.

Smaller observations:
- Events captured inside a handler (`/iso/:tag`) have `transaction: null`; the isolation scope's transaction name is only set from `onAfterHandle`/`onError`, which run after the handler body. Errors thrown from the handler are fine because `onError` sets the name before capturing.
- In static lifecycle the `AfterResponse` phase span never appears in `spans[]` (the root span has already ended); in stream lifecycle it does appear. Not wrong, just an asymmetry worth knowing when comparing lifecycles.
- The SDK's own hooks show up as user-visible spans named `sentryOnRequest`, `sentryOnAfterHandle`, `sentryOnError`. The source calls this a deliberate tradeoff; it is noise in every single trace.
- Span envelopes flush on a ~5s timer even in stream lifecycle, so span assertions need the same sentinel discipline as logs.
- Contradiction with the established Bun fact "no library spans without a `@sentry/bun/plugin` bundle": `mysql2` does produce db spans under plain `bun app.ts`, because modern `mysql2` publishes `node:diagnostics_channel` events itself (`node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js`) and the SDK subscribes to them. The rule still holds for drivers that need the injected channels — `mysql`@2 gave nothing until the plugin build.
- Cleanup done: all bun/node processes killed, `node_modules` removed (122M). Ports used: 41371-41375 (apps), 41999 (sink).

notes:
Corrections to the task's setup hint: (a) `@sentry/elysia`'s `withElysia` DOES load and work on workerd. Its own source only imports `@sentry/core` and `@sentry/conventions`; the `@sentry/bun` re-export sits in the package index and esbuild tree-shakes it away when you import just `withElysia`. Only `init` from `@sentry/elysia` is unusable there (sdk.js imports `node:os`, `global.process.env`, and `@sentry/bun`'s init). (b) Plain `withSentry` around `app.fetch` is the strictly worse option: no route names and, worse, zero error events, because Elysia's default error handling turns the throw into a 500 response before it can reach the Worker's fetch handler.

Ordering trap worth a docs callout: `withElysia` installs its route-naming hook with `.onAfterHandle({ as: 'global' })`. On workerd with `aot: false`, that hook does not reach routes that were already registered, so `withElysia(appWithRoutes)` names only the error path. `withElysia(new Elysia({aot:false})).get(...)` names everything. On Bun this ordering probably does not matter (the Bun branch of `app.wrap` owns the root span); it does here.

No Elysia lifecycle spans on Cloudflare. `platform-includes/.../javascript.elysia.mdx:3-5` promises spans for Request/Parse/Transform/BeforeHandle/Handle/AfterHandle/MapResponse/AfterResponse/Error with `op: request_handler.elysia` / `middleware.elysia`; on workerd every transaction came back with `spans: []` except the `http.client` fetch span. The `app.trace()` handler that creates them depends on `rootSpanForRequest`, which is only populated by the Bun branch of `app.wrap`.

Tarball hazard for whoever reruns this: `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz` and `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz` are older than `$REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-cloudflare-10.67.0.tgz`. Repacking core, opentelemetry, cloudflare and server-utils from $W fixed it. Also, `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-elysia-...tgz` needs `sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz` on the same command line or it fails with `notarget No matching version found for @sentry/server-runtime-injection@10.67.0`.

Elysia runs on Deno unchanged: `new Elysia().get(...)` mounted with `Deno.serve({port}, app.fetch)`, deno.json `{"nodeModulesDir":"manual"}`, deps installed with npm. Two Sentry wirings exist and they behave very differently.

(A) The wiring a docs page would show today (@sentry/elysia, the documented package):
  npm install elysia@1 mysql@2 $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{elysia,bun,node,core,deno,opentelemetry,server-utils,server-runtime-injection}-10.67.0.tgz
  instrument.ts: `import "@sentry/deno/import";` then `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/elysia"; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static'|'stream' })`
  app.ts: `import "./instrument.ts";` as the first line, `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia()).get(...)`, `Deno.serve({port,hostname}, app.fetch)`
  run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys --allow-ffi app.ts`
  This loads and inits fine but is BROKEN for tracing/isolation: withElysia's `isBun()` guard is false on Deno, so it takes the Node branch that assumes an HTTP-instrumentation root span, and @sentry/bun does not instrument Deno.serve. Result: no root span, no isolation scope, no continueTrace.

(B) The wiring that actually works, but is not reachable through any public export:
  `import "@sentry/deno/import"; import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno"; Sentry.init({...})` plus
  `import { withElysia } from "./node_modules/@sentry/elysia/build/esm/withElysia.js";`
  @sentry/deno instruments Deno.serve and supplies the root span + isolation scope, and withElysia's Node branch then works exactly as intended. A docs page cannot show this today because @sentry/elysia's package entry re-exports all of @sentry/bun, and @sentry/deno exports no withElysia. Shipping it would need a `@sentry/elysia/deno` subpath or a withElysia re-export from @sentry/deno.

notes:
Root cause of the (A) failures is one line in packages/elysia/src/withElysia.ts: `function isBun() { return typeof Bun !== 'undefined'; }` gates the whole root-span / withIsolationScope / continueTrace block. On Deno that is false, so withElysia falls through to the Node branch `const activeSpan = getActiveSpan(); if (activeSpan) rootSpanForRequest.set(...)`, which silently does nothing because @sentry/bun does not instrument Deno.serve. Nothing warns; the app looks instrumented (spans do arrive) but every lifecycle span is its own root segment and the whole process shares one trace and one isolation scope for its entire lifetime. The condition should be "no HTTP-server instrumentation created a root span" rather than "is Bun". @sentry/deno already provides that root span and isolation scope, which is what makes (B) work end to end.

Second bug seen in (A): events are tagged `sdk: sentry.javascript.bun` and `contexts.runtime.name: bun` while running on Deno. In packages/elysia/src/sdk.ts the object `options` is spread from `userOptions` BEFORE `applySdkMetadata(userOptions, 'elysia', ...)` runs, so the elysia metadata never reaches the client and the bun SDK identity survives; `getRuntime()` correctly returns a non-bun runtime but the runtime context is overwritten downstream by @sentry/bun.

Third: withElysia is reachable only through @sentry/elysia's package entry, which re-exports the entirety of @sentry/bun. So the working Deno configuration cannot be written by a user following any public API; it needs a deep import into build/esm/withElysia.js. A `@sentry/elysia/deno` subpath (or re-exporting withElysia from @sentry/deno) would make (B) documentable.

Environment notes: mysql2 is unusable on Deno whenever the @sentry/deno import hook is loaded (K3 confirmed, mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13 requires a JSON file); mysql@2 works. Ports 43711 (sink), 43712 (app A), 43713 (recorder), 43714 (app B), 41338 (bare) were used; 41337 was already held by another agent. All four processes were killed and node_modules (123M) removed.

notes:
Verdicts come from the bundled run; every capability reproduced in both `stream` and `static`, and I noted the two places the lifecycles disagree (http.client span naming, span-vs-transaction envelope shape).

The headline finding for this cell is the bundle boundary, not any single capability. Express on bun has two distinct behaviours on the same SDK build:
- `bun app.ts` / `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts`: transaction source `url` (`GET /users/42`), no middleware/handler spans, no db span, and NO error event for a throwing route unless `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)` is added (which then reports mechanism `auto.middleware.express`). Logs and the node:http server span still work. The SDK emits no warning about the missing instrumentation unless `debug: true`.
- `bun dist/app.js` built with `Bun.build({ external: ["@sentry/*"], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })`: bundler reports `["express","mysql"]`, source `route`, full middleware/handler/db span tree, and automatic error capture with mechanism `auto.http.express` — setupExpressErrorHandler becomes unnecessary and does not double-report.

So the answer to the setup hint's question: setupExpressErrorHandler is REQUIRED only on the un-bundled path and OPTIONAL (safe, non-duplicating) on the bundled path. A docs page should still show it, because it is the only thing that makes the un-bundled quick start capture errors at all.

Other details worth carrying forward:
- `external: ["@sentry/*"]` matters: it is what lets the process-wide client from the un-bundled instrument.ts and the injected channels in the bundle agree on one client.
- The mysql connection is at module scope, per known finding K11; I did not re-derive the in-request case.
- Express itself needs no adaptation to run on bun: express@4.22.1 with plain `app.listen()` serves correctly with no Sentry present.
- The middleware span named `middleware query2` (not `query`) shows up in every trace. That is express 4's own `query` middleware, and the trailing `2` looks like a name-collision suffix from the instrumentation — cosmetic, but odd enough to mention.
- Environmental snag, not a finding: port 41338 was already held by another agent's server and bun reported `error: Failed to start server. Is port 41338 in use?`. I switched to ephemeral ports (`PORT=0`) for the app and 47231 for the sink.
- Cleanup done: every started process killed by captured pid, `rm -rf node_modules` in the task dir; the dir is now 3.6M (mostly dist/app.js plus logs).

notes:
Headline: Express 5 runs on Workers today and the develop @sentry/cloudflare SDK covers it better than expected — async context propagates cleanly through the `cloudflare:node` httpServerHandler bridge, so isolation, trace continuation, scope tags and child spans all work inside express handlers with no extra wiring. But two things stand between this and a docs page.

1. BUG (blocking): with the Cloudflare Vite plugin's default `buildTimeInstrumentation: true`, the canonical Express entry — `app.get(...)` and `app.listen()` at module scope, exactly what every Express docs page shows — crashes the Worker at startup with `Disallowed operation called within global scope … generating random values are not allowed within global scope`. The injected wrapper around `Router.prototype.route` finds live channel subscribers during module evaluation and runs the Sentry subscriber (which mints a span id) at global scope. Confirmed by a control build: the same top-level entry with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ buildTimeInstrumentation: false })` boots fine, and the same entry under plain `wrangler dev` boots fine. Workaround used here is to defer `express()` + route registration + `listen()` into the first request. Either the express subscriber must not start a span for route registration, or `route`/`Router.prototype[method]` should not be an instrumented operation at all.

2. Sharp cliff between the two run shapes. Plain `wrangler dev` gives raw-URL transaction names (`GET /users/42`, source `url`) and silently swallows every route error — the only signal is a transaction with `status: internal_error` and no event. That is the shape a user lands on if they follow the Cloudflare quickstart and add express themselves. Everything good (route templates, `handler` spans, automatic `auto.http.express` error capture, db spans) requires Vite + the Sentry plugin. A docs page must lead with the Vite shape.

Smaller observations:
- mysql2 needs `disableEval: true` to run on workerd at all (`EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`). Unrelated to Sentry but any db example on this runtime has to say so.
- Under traceLifecycle 'stream' the http.server span carries `http.route: /users/:id` but no `sentry.source` attribute at all; the name is already parameterized, so this may be intentional, flagging it for the span-name owner.
- `vite build` emits an `assets` entry that makes `wrangler dev --config dist/.../wrangler.json` fail with `The directory specified by the "assets.directory" field … does not exist: dist/client` on a rebuild-triggered reload. Creating an empty `dist/client` works around it. Possibly a @cloudflare/vite-plugin quirk for asset-less workers, not a Sentry issue.
- Not tested: `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` (withSentry was enough), Durable Objects, deployed (non-local) workerd.

Without the import hook the error is NOT captured at all — Express's default error handler swallows it and only Deno's stderr shows the stack. Importing `setupExpressErrorHandler` from `@sentry/server-utils` restores capture without the hook (mechanism `auto.middleware.express`), but `@sentry/deno` does not re-export it, so there is no supported no-hook path. notes:
Headline finding: Express on Deno is fully instrumentable on develop, but only via a workaround that no user could guess.

1. denoland/deno#36240 (K3) is confirmed and is fatal on Express: `import "@sentry/deno/import"` makes `require('./codes.json')` in `statuses` throw `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`, so Express never imports. Express 5 crashes in `statuses`; the failure is not Express-specific but hits it first.

2. The "second load hook" fix works completely. A 6-line user-land `Module.registerHooks({ load })` that forces `format: "json"` for `.json` URLs (registered AFTER `@sentry/deno/import`) makes the entire path work: Express boots, and errors, route names, handler spans, isolation, incoming trace continuation, db spans and logs all behave. This is a small enough patch that the SDK could plausibly ship it inside `registerDiagnosticsChannelInjection()` for Deno (packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:123, the `mod.registerHooks({ resolve, load })` branch) rather than leaving it to users. That is the single highest-value fix for this cell.

3. The no-hook path is silently degraded, not just less detailed. Without the hook the SDK captures NOTHING for a thrown route error — Express's default handler swallows it and no warning is printed. Combined with the fact that the docs' Deno snippet is exactly the no-hook snippet, a user following the docs today gets an Express app whose 500s are invisible in Sentry.

4. `setupExpressErrorHandler` is exported from `@sentry/server-utils` (packages/server-utils/src/index.ts:56) but is not re-exported from `@sentry/deno` (packages/deno/src/index.ts has no such export). It works when imported from `@sentry/server-utils` directly (mechanism `auto.middleware.express`), so re-exporting it would give Deno users a supported no-hook fallback.

5. Outgoing `fetch` (K2) is the one hard gap: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` on the wire, so an Express handler on Deno cannot continue a trace downstream. `@sentry/deno` ships `denoHttpIntegration`, so `node:http` clients are the only propagating option today.

6. `expressIntegration()` is already in the Deno default integration set (packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:48 via `getTracingIntegrations()`); it needed no explicit `integrations: []` entry.

7. Not re-derived (established in TOOLBOX): Deno fetch span/header gap (K2), Deno json-require crash (K3). Everything else above was observed in this run on Deno 2.9.0 / Express 5.2.1 / router 2.x / develop @ 10.67.0 via worktree symlinks.

notes:
Headline: the setup hint is right — Fastify needs no Bun plugin build. Fastify publishes its own diagnostics channels, and the develop SDK subscribes to them directly, so plain `bun app.mjs` already gives route-named server transactions with source `route`, unhandled-error capture with `auto.function.fastify`, per-request isolation, trace continuation, http.client spans with propagation headers, and logs. This contradicts the toolbox's own Bun bullet ("It records NO library spans (databases, AI, Express, Koa, Hapi, Fastify)"): for Fastify on Bun 1.4.0 that is no longer true, and it is the single most docs-relevant finding here. Express on Bun presumably still needs the bundle; Fastify does not.

The bundle is needed for exactly one of the seven capabilities: db spans. mysql@2 at module scope is invisible on plain `bun run` and produces `db SELECT id, name FROM users` under `sentryBunPlugin()`. The SDK emits no warning about the missing instrumentation without `debug: true`, so a user gets a Fastify app that looks fully instrumented and silently has no database visibility — the most likely real-world trap for this combination.

Span shape: every request carries two child spans, `handler GET /<route>` and `handler fastify - route-handler`. Not a duplicate; they are the request-handler and route-handler hook spans. Both have op `handler` and neither carries a `sentry.source` attribute in the stream envelope, so in stream lifecycle only the parent `http.server` span is route-named.

Stream vs static: identical verdicts for all seven capabilities. Errors, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing fetch and logs were all confirmed under stream (run A) and re-confirmed under static (runs B and C); route-name `source: route` is only directly assertable under static (`transaction_info.source`), which is why the route-names verdict is quoted from runs B/C. db spans confirmed under static in run C, absence confirmed under both A and B.

One naming difference worth flagging to whoever writes the guide: the outgoing client span is `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` in stream lifecycle (the new low-cardinality naming) but `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41338/hit` in static. Same span, different name depending on lifecycle.

notes:
The blocker is workerd's ban on dynamic code generation, a platform invariant with no compatibility flag. It is not a Sentry issue and not a wiring issue. Fastify's router (find-my-way) compiles path matchers, params builders and constraint deriving with `new Function` at route-registration time, so `app.get('/users/:id', ...)` throws before any request is served. Fastify 4 (find-my-way 7.7.0) has the same four call sites, so downgrading is not an escape. Fastify would additionally hit the same wall in `ajv` (schema validation) and `fast-json-stringify` (response serialization) as soon as any route schema is declared.

A nuance worth recording for the other Cloudflare cells: `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` + `httpServerHandler` itself works fine on this workerd (the control worker served 200s), but most Node frameworks cannot be constructed at module scope, because workerd forbids random-value generation, timers and async I/O in global scope. notes:
Headline: Fastify on Deno is the best-behaved framework/runtime pair I would expect from this matrix — six of seven capabilities work with zero build step and zero extra configuration, and the one failure (outgoing `fetch`) is a pre-existing Deno-wide gap (K2), not a Fastify problem.

Two findings worth a docs page:

1. The instrumentation mechanism is diagnostics channels that Fastify and mysql2 publish themselves, so the Deno import hook is not just unnecessary, it is harmful. `fastifyIntegration()` subscribes to `fastify.initialization` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/fastify/instrumentation.ts, comment at the `instrumentFastifyInstance` JSDoc), and it is already in `getErrorIntegrations()` (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/index.ts:60), which the Deno SDK includes by default (packages/deno/src/sdk.ts). Likewise `mysql2-dc-subscriber.ts` subscribes to `mysql2:query`/`mysql2:execute`/`mysql2:connect`/`mysql2:pool:connect`, published by mysql2 >= 3.20.0. That is why db spans appeared with no hook and no bundler — which is important, because K3 makes the hook unusable here.

2. K3 is reproduced exactly and is fatal, not degraded: adding `import "@sentry/deno/import";` makes the process die at import with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` from `ajv/dist/core.js:21` doing `require("./refs/data.json")`. Any docs page that tells Deno users to add the import hook for library instrumentation would break every Fastify app. Deno bug denoland/deno#36240.

Other observations:
- `setupFastifyErrorHandler(app)` is a documented step in the Fastify/Node guide but is a no-op on develop (packages/server-utils/src/integrations/fastify/index.ts, `@deprecated Remove this call`). Errors were captured without it.
- Both fastify spans per request are `handler` op: one `<pluginName> - route-handler` wrapper and one route-URL-named span. Under stream lifecycle the sink shows them both as `handler | /users/:id`; under static as `handler GET /users/:id` + `handler fastify - route-handler`.
- The `http.client` span from `node:http` is named `GET 127.0.0.1` (low-cardinality naming from the recent `feat: Emit low-cardinality http.client span names for node:http and undici` commit), not the full URL.
- Ports 41337 (my first sink pick) was already taken by another agent; I moved to 47021/47022/47025 and 41339.
- Everything ran on `deno` 2.9.0; I did not additionally exercise the CI pin at `$SCRATCH/deno283/deno`.
- Processes killed and `node_modules` removed before returning.

setup:
Fresh 2 builds with Deno/Vite but the built server runs on bun unchanged. Exact wiring:

1. Scaffold + build with deno (deno is only a build-time tool here):
   `deno run -A -r jsr:@fresh/init@2 ./app --force --tailwind`
   `cd app && deno task build`  ->  `_fresh/server.js` which is literally
   `import server from "./server/server-entry.mjs"; export default { fetch: server.fetch };`
   The SSR bundle has zero bare imports by default, so bun needs nothing from Deno at runtime.
   Only `Deno.serve` (used by `app.listen()`, not by the default export), `Deno.stat`/`Deno.open`
   (static-file serving) and `Deno.readTextFileSync` (error code frames, inside try/catch) survive
   in the bundle, so the `fetch` path is Deno-free.

2. Keep the SDK and the db driver out of the SSR bundle so bun resolves them at runtime.
   app/vite.config.ts:
     export default defineConfig({
       plugins: [fresh(), tailwindcss()],
       ssr: { external: ["@sentry/bun", "mysql2", "mysql2/promise"] },
       build: { rollupOptions: { external: [/^@sentry\//, /^mysql2/] } },
     });

3. Install the SDK in the PARENT directory of the Fresh app (not in app/, whose node_modules is
   Deno-managed and gets pruned by npm). Bun resolves bare imports by walking up from the bundled
   file at app/_fresh/server/assets/*.js, so a node_modules one level above app/ is found:
     npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz \
       $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz \
       $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz mysql2

4. instrument.ts (parent dir):
     import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
     Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel: "http://127.0.0.1:<sink>/", tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "stream"|"static" });

5. entry.ts (parent dir) - init first, then the Fresh bundle, then Bun.serve:
     import "./instrument.ts";
     import server from "./app/_fresh/server.js";

notes:
Key findings a docs page would have to carry:

1. Fresh 2 on bun is real and needs no shim. The Vite SSR build emits `_fresh/server.js` as
   `export default { fetch }` with zero bare imports, which is exactly Bun.serve's entry shape.
   Deno is only a build-time dependency. `Deno.serve` in the bundle sits inside `app.listen()`,
   which the default export never calls. The Deno-only bits that DO remain on a hot path are
   `Deno.stat`/`Deno.open` in Fresh's static-file serving, so `/assets/*` under bun is the one
   thing I would expect to break; I did not exercise it (the HTML references the asset, I only
   asserted on the SSR HTML and the route handlers).

2. Installing the SDK is the non-obvious step. The Fresh app dir's node_modules is Deno-managed
   (`nodeModulesDir: "manual"`, no package.json), and `npm install` there prunes the Vite/preact
   tree the build needs. Putting node_modules one directory ABOVE the app works because bun
   resolves bare specifiers by walking up from app/_fresh/server/assets/*.js. A docs page should
   either say that, or tell users to add a real package.json to the Fresh app.

3. @sentry/bun and the db driver must be `ssr.external` in vite.config.ts. If they are bundled
   into server-entry.js, Sentry.init in the bundle would run a second copy of the SDK and the
   diagnostics-channel injection has nothing to hook.

4. Both defects here are "framework has no Sentry integration" defects, and both have the same
   one-middleware fix, which is what a Fresh guide would need to ship:
   - Fresh swallows route-handler throws entirely (500 page, span status internal_error, no event).
   - The Bun.serve span is named from the raw URL (`GET /users/42`, source url), never from the
     matched pattern. Fresh does expose `ctx.route` (= "/users/:id"), so the data is available.
   Note the source inconsistency after `updateSpanName`: stream lifecycle reports source "route",
   static lifecycle reports "custom", and setting `sentry.source` back to "route" after
   updateSpanName does not stick in static.

5. Contradicts the standing Bun note that library spans need a `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin`
   bundle: mysql2 spans came through on plain `bun entry.ts` with origin
   auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel. What mattered was module-scope pool creation reached from
   the server entry (app/dbpool.ts imported by main.ts), not a build-time plugin. Worth
   re-checking on the plain Bun/express template, since it changes the recommended setup.

6. One transient during the very first bun run: `/api/:name` 404'd on the first request after
   boot while `/` succeeded, and the request never reached the logger middleware. It did not
   reproduce on any later run (same bundle, same command). Likely a race between Bun's server
   accepting connections and Fresh's lazy fs-route module import; I did not chase it further and
   would not report it as a finding without a repro.

notes:
- Fresh 2 needed no adapter. Its vite build already emits `export default { fetch: server.fetch }` (for `deno serve`), which is exactly the Workers module shape, so `withSentry` wraps it directly. No Deno global is touched on the request path for API/page routes — `Deno.serve`/`Deno.build` live only in `App.listen()`, and `import.meta.dirname` reaching the ProdBuildCache root did not throw at module eval under workerd.
- The one Deno-only path that does matter is `staticFiles()`, whose ProdBuildCache `readFile` calls `Deno.stat`/`Deno.open`. I removed that middleware; a real deployment needs Workers Assets. Page rendering itself works (the /boom error page rendered full HTML with the emitted stylesheet link).
- Keeping `@sentry/cloudflare` external to the Fresh SSR bundle is load-bearing: if it were bundled, routes calling `Sentry.setTag`/`captureException` would talk to a second SDK copy with no client. With `external`, wrangler's esbuild resolves both the worker entry and the route chunks to the same node_modules copy. esbuild prints a harmless `[ignored-bare-import] "sideEffects": false` warning for `import "@sentry/cloudflare"` in each route chunk.
- The most interesting gap is route names: nothing in @sentry/cloudflare knows about Fresh's router, so every span is either `GET /users/42` (static, source url) or bare `GET` (stream). Fresh exposes the matched pattern on the context, so a five-line middleware fixes it, but it lands as source `custom` because `updateSpanName` overrides the source. A Fresh integration setting source `route` would be the real fix.
- db spans are doubly blocked on this runtime: mysql2 cannot run on workerd at all (`new Function` is disallowed), and the only instrumentation path that exists for Cloudflare (build-time channel injection) requires the driver inside the bundle, which is exactly what breaks it via `createRequire(import.meta.url)` in Vite's CJS interop. mysql@2 external is the only combination that queries successfully, and it gets no spans.
- I did not use @cloudflare/vite-plugin; Fresh's own vite build plus plain `wrangler dev` was enough, which also means `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin`'s autoInstrumentation half (worker-entry wrapping from wrangler config) has no environment to attach to here and must be disabled.
- Cleanup done: wrangler/workerd, sink and recorder processes killed (pids 89846, 89407, 2672, 16625, 89830, 89831, 89845, 93354; all three ports verified free), and app/node_modules removed (327M). The dir is left at 4.9M with sources, the built `_fresh/` output and the logs. Reinstall with the npm line above to rerun.
- Ports used: sink 22984, recorder 20504, wrangler 58164. Two earlier picks (41777, 47311) were already held by other agents' sinks; I moved rather than touching them.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: Fresh swallows every route error: App.handler() catches it and returns the 500 from DEFAULT_ERROR_HANDLER, so it never escapes to Deno.serve/node:http and Sentry's own handlers never see it. With no middleware, GET /api/boom produced only a 500 transaction and no event at all. The only mechanism that works is a user middleware that wraps `await ctx.next()` in try/catch, calls Sentry.captureException and rethrows; with it the event arrives in both vite dev and the `deno serve _fresh/server.js` build (mechanism is whatever you pass, here `fresh.middleware`, handled false), carries a context line, and shares the request's trace id.

notes:
Fresh 2 runs on Deno without Sentry in all three shapes tested (vite dev, `deno task build`, `deno serve -A _fresh/server.js`), so viability was never in doubt; the interesting result is how much hand-wiring the SDK needs.

What a Fresh docs page would have to say that no existing page says:
- Fresh catches all route errors in App.handler() (src/app.ts:491-494) and in its `_error` command chain, so error capture is impossible without a user middleware that rethrows. There is no `app.onError(handler)` hook that gives Sentry the error; `App.onError(path, routeOrMiddleware)` is a route-shaped 500 page, and the internal `setErrorInterceptor` is not exported from `fresh`'s mod.ts.
- Fresh already writes the route name onto the active OTEL span (src/app.ts:444-447) and opens `middlewares` / `render` / route spans through `tracer.startActiveSpan` (src/middlewares/mod.ts:143, src/render.ts:31, src/context.ts:344). None of it reaches Sentry. @sentry/deno does register a global OTEL TracerProvider (sdk.ts:115 -> opentelemetry/tracer.ts), but `trace.getActiveSpan()` needs a ContextManager, which Sentry does not install, and in dev the app resolves a second copy of @opentelemetry/api (Deno's `.deno` layout vs the one under node_modules), so the calls land on NoopTracer. Making Sentry a real OTEL context/tracer host on Deno would give Fresh route names and framework spans for free.
- `@sentry/deno` does not export `wrapDenoRequestHandler`, so there is no supported way to instrument a `deno serve` default export by hand. It happened to work here only because `deno serve` calls the JS `Deno.serve` after the entry module ran, so the `denoServeIntegration` proxy was already in place.

Two defects worth filing:
1. Isolation-scope/current-scope leak in the `deno serve` production shape: a `Sentry.setTag` in one request shows up on every later request's events and transactions in the same process (verified sequentially, not just under concurrency). The same code under the vite dev / node:http path does not leak. Concurrent requests still each saw their own tag, so this looks like an async-context restore problem around `withIsolationScope`/`withScope` on the Deno.serve path rather than a plain global-scope write.
2. In vite dev the very first request to a cold server produces no server span at all, because `main.ts` (and therefore `Sentry.init`) is only loaded by the SSR runner when that first request arrives, after the node:http span would have started. Every later request is fine.

Also confirmed from the toolbox list, unchanged: K2 (Deno outgoing fetch gets neither a span nor propagation headers) and K3 (with the import hook active, `mysql2` dies on `require('*.json')` with `Unexpected token ':'`; `mysql@2` is the only driver that works).

Everything ran against develop tarballs only; 10.73.0 was never installed. Processes started (sink 52413, dev 52520/52540, `deno serve` 52530) were all killed and the ports verified free. `sdkdeps/node_modules` and `app/node_modules` were removed afterwards (the dir is down from 122M to 2.3M); the reinstall commands above restore both.

import * as Sentry from "@sentry/bun";
Sentry.init({ dsn: "...", tracesSampleRate: 1.0 /*, traceLifecycle: "static" */ });

await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["./app.ts"], outdir: "./dist", target: "bun",

Counterfactual (matters for the docs): plain `bun app.ts` / `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` gives NO hapi instrumentation at all — transactions are `GET /users/42` with `source: "url"`, no `router` span, no `db` span, and the handler error is **not captured at all** (silently swallowed by hapi's 500). notes:
Three things a docs page for this combination would have to say, and none of them are written down anywhere today:

1. Hapi route handler errors are invisible on Cloudflare. `hapiIntegration()` from @sentry/server-utils is not in @sentry/cloudflare's default integration set and is not re-exported from @sentry/cloudflare, so a user must import it from @sentry/server-utils by hand. Even then it does not work: the integration subscribes to `orchestrion:@hapi/hapi:start` / `:initialize`, `attachHapiErrorHandler` does run (state flag confirmed true on `server.events`), but the `{name:'request', channels:['error']}` podium event that the handler listens for never fires under workerd. A plain listener I registered on the same event never fired either, so Hapi's deferred emit is being dropped by the Workers I/O context, not by Sentry. The only recipe that captures is an `onPreResponse` extension. Worth a Sentry-side decision: either document the extension, or have the hapi integration hook a synchronous path (e.g. the `ext`/`route` channel error context) instead of the podium event.

2. `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` breaks module-scope Hapi route registration. The injected `tr_ch_apm$route.start.runStores(...)` wrapper around `Server.prototype.route` starts a Sentry span, which generates random values, which workerd forbids in global scope. Every Hapi-on-Workers example on the internet registers routes at module scope, so adding the plugin turns a working Worker into one that fails to boot with a message that names neither Sentry nor Hapi. The same is likely true of any framework whose setup calls an injected channel at module scope. Control build without the Sentry plugin boots fine, so the plugin is the cause.

3. Package-resolution trap for anyone following a tarball/local-build workflow: `@sentry/cloudflare` imports `@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels`, and npm happily resolves `@sentry/opentelemetry@10.67.0` from the registry (the released v10 build) next to a develop-built `@sentry/core@10.67.0`, which then fails the vite/esbuild bundle with `No matching export in "@sentry/core/build/esm/index.js" for import "spanShouldInferOtelSource"`. Both tarballs must be passed on the install command line.

Runtime facts worth recording elsewhere in the matrix: mysql2 is unusable on workerd ("Code generation from strings disallowed for this context") while mysql@2 works, including a module-scope pool reaching 127.0.0.1:3307. Hapi 21 itself needs nothing beyond `nodejs_compat` + `enable_nodejs_http_server_modules` and `httpServerHandler({ port })` - it booted and served parameterized routes on the very first try with no Sentry present.

notes:
Viability: Hapi imports and serves on Deno with no Sentry at all (bare.ts started and answered GET /users/{id}), and also boots fine with Sentry.init alone. The only thing that breaks it is the diagnostics-channel import hook.

The headline finding is that on Deno the Hapi story is all-or-nothing and gated on a runtime bug. Without `import "@sentry/deno/import"` you get no route names, no db spans, and — worst — no error event at all for a route handler throw, because Hapi turns it into a Boom 500 and nothing else observes it. With the hook you get all three, but the app does not start: @hapi/validate/lib/common.js:6 does `require('../package.json')` and Deno compiles JSON through the CJS compiler as soon as any Module.registerHooks load hook is registered (denoland/deno#36240, K3). The 12-line json-fix.mjs closes that gap completely and nothing else was needed; @hapi/hapi, @hapi/validate, @hapi/hoek and the rest all loaded and every capability except fetch worked. That workaround is small enough that the SDK could ship it inside @sentry/deno/import — the hook already owns the load chain, and short-circuiting `.json` there costs nothing on Node — which would make Hapi (and, per K3, Express and Fastify) work on Deno out of the box.

Fetch is the one genuine gap and it is not Hapi's. The same handler that gets a full http.client span with sentry-trace and baggage from node:http.get gets nothing at all from fetch(), in both lifecycles and with and without the hook. Any Hapi app on Deno that calls a downstream service with fetch has a broken distributed trace.

Other observations: the docs' `Sentry.setupHapiErrorHandler(server)` step is both unnecessary and unavailable on develop's @sentry/deno — hapiIntegration comes in as a default via getErrorIntegrations()/getTracingIntegrations() from @sentry/server-utils. Route naming survives both lifecycles: static reports source "route" with a nested `router GET /users/{id}` span, stream reports `http.server GET /users/{id}`. Isolation was clean under three concurrent staggered requests in every configuration. Ports used: sink 45903, recorder 45907, Hapi on port 0 (several ports in the 38000-47000 range were already held by other agents, hence port 0 for the app). All processes started here were killed before returning; node_modules was kept because it is only 3.3 MB and makes the probe rerunnable.

runtime: Bun 1.4.0 (`bun`), both unbundled (`bun app.ts`) and as a `Bun.build` bundle with `sentryBunPlugin`

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: An error thrown in `app.get('/boom')` is captured with mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`, handled=false, transaction `GET /boom`, and stack frames with context lines; the transaction is marked `internal_error`. Hono's default onError still returns 500 to the client, so the error is not swallowed from Sentry's point of view - the middleware reads `context.error` in its response handler. Identical unbundled and bundled, in both `static` and `stream` lifecycle.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: `GET /users/:id` with `source: "route"` and `http.route: /users/:id` on the server span, from the parameterized Hono route. In `traceLifecycle: 'static'` it is the transaction name; in `stream` the `http.server` span is named `GET /users/:id` and carries `http.route`. No method-only fallback, so the Hono middleware's route resolution overrides the bare Bun.serve naming.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent `GET /iso/:tag` requests (each `Sentry.setTag('req-tag', ...)`, then a 150-250ms await, then `captureException`) produced three events each carrying only its own tag and its own trace id, and three transactions with the matching tag and trace id. No cross-talk. Lifecycle: static.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request with `sentry-trace: aaaa...-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus baggage yields a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. Same in stream lifecycle (trace `cccc...`, parent `dddddddddddddddd`). Lifecycle: static and stream.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: `fetch()` from inside a handler to a local recorder produced a child span `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41802/rec` under `GET /fetchout` (static) / low-cardinality `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` in stream, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: <same trace id>-<span id>-1` plus a full baggage header including `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Ffetchout`. Note this contrasts with Deno finding K2.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: Module-scope `mysql2@3.24.3` connection queried inside a handler gives `db SELECT * FROM users` (static) / `db SELECT users` (stream) WITHOUT any bundle - mysql2 >=3.x publishes `mysql2:query` tracing channels itself and the SDK's DC subscriber picks them up under plain `bun app.ts`. Legacy `mysql@2` gives NO span unbundled and DOES get `db SELECT * FROM users` after a `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin()`. So the Bun plugin build is needed only for drivers without native diagnostics_channel; for mysql2 it is optional.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: `Sentry.logger.info('hono-bun-log-line', { where: 'handler' })` inside a handler arrives as a `log` envelope item `info: hono-bun-log-line` about 5s later (timer flush). Works unbundled and bundled; no `enableLogs` option needed on develop.

capabilities.name: client errors
capabilities.detail: No browser surface in this cell - Hono on Bun is a server-only app, so there is no client-side SDK to probe.

- ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12 — "The `@sentry/hono` SDK supports Hono 4+ across multiple runtimes: Cloudflare Workers, Node.js, Bun, and Deno."

- .../hono/index.mdx:290-317 — Bun tab of the setup snippet: `import { sentry } from "@sentry/hono/bun"`, `app.use(sentry(app, { dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, dataCollection: {...} }))`, `export default app;`. - ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx:96-98 — the general Bun guide carries an Alert titled "Bundled Code Limitation": "Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code, including Bun's single-file executables ... you'll need to manually instrument your code instead of relying on auto-instrumentation." On develop this is backwards for library spans: bundling with `sentryBunPlugin` is exactly what makes `mysql@2` produce spans, and the unbundled run is the one that misses them. `sentryBunPlugin` does not appear anywhere under ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs or ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes.
- No page anywhere pairs Hono with Bun beyond the tab above; the Bun guide never mentions Hono (`grep -rn -i hono docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` is empty).
- Disagreement between docs and package README: ~/dev/sentry-worktrees/audit-runtime-docs/packages/hono/README.md:172-190 shows the Bun setup ending in `import { serve } from '@hono/node-server'; ... serve(app);`, which is the Node recipe pasted into the Bun section. The docs page's `export default app` is the correct Bun form and is what I ran.
notes:
Headline: Hono on Bun is the strongest of the non-Node runtimes I saw here — every one of the seven capabilities passed, unbundled, with the single middleware line the docs already show. Nothing was broken or partial.

Two findings worth acting on:

1. The "Bun needs a bundle for library spans" rule is now driver-dependent, not blanket. `mysql2@3.24.3` ships its own `node:diagnostics_channel` tracing channels (`node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js:9-31`, channels `mysql2:query` / `mysql2:execute` / `mysql2:connect`), and the SDK's `@sentry/server-utils` mysql2 DC subscriber picks them up under plain `bun app.ts`. Legacy `mysql@2` has no such channels and stays silent until built with `sentryBunPlugin`. This softens the established Bun fact ("records NO library spans") — it is true for build-time-injected drivers, false for drivers with native DC. Any docs page should say which case a reader is in rather than "bundle or nothing".

2. Bundle boundary: `external: ['@sentry/*']` (the shape the toolbox lists for the generic Bun app) is actively wrong for Hono, because it leaves `hono` inside the bundle and `@sentry/hono` outside, so the prototype patches land on a different Hono instance. Bundling everything (`Bun.build` with no `external`) worked for all seven capabilities including the Hono route names. Worth stating explicitly in the docs if a bundle recipe is ever added.

Other observations:
- `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` (the develop default) already carries `http.route` and the `GET /users/:id` name on the `http.server` span, so route naming does not depend on choosing `static`. Stream also shows the new low-cardinality client names (`http.client GET 127.0.0.1`, `db SELECT users`) versus static's full descriptions.
- The error mechanism is `auto.http.hono.context_error`, i.e. the middleware reads `c.error` after `await next()`. An error thrown by a middleware registered *before* `sentry(app, ...)` would not reach that check; I did not probe that ordering.
- Cleanup: all five server processes killed (pids captured in `*.pid`), no listeners left on 41733/41799-41802, and `node_modules` (118M) removed. `dist/` and the source files remain.

Gap: the page never mentions Vite, `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`, `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin` or `buildTimeInstrumentation` (grep for vite/mysql/database over the file only hits :162, which is about Node.js). So a Hono-on-CF user following the docs verbatim gets errors, routes, isolation, trace propagation, fetch spans and logs, but silently gets no database spans, and the docs give them no hint that a Vite build is what turns those on. notes:
Viability was never in doubt for the framework itself — Hono is the canonical CF Workers framework and served requests immediately; there was no need for a Sentry-free control run.

Findings worth flagging:
- `sentry(app, options)` works by mutation: it calls `withSentry(cb, app)` from @sentry/cloudflare, and withSentry mutates `handler.fetch/scheduled/queue/...` in place and returns the same object, which is why `export default app` (not `export default withSentry(...)`) is correct. Source: node_modules/@sentry/hono/build/esm/cloudflare/middleware.js and @sentry/cloudflare/build/esm/dev/withSentry.js.
- The CF middleware always strips the Hono integration from user + default integrations (`buildFilteredIntegrations(honoOptions.integrations, true)`) because withSentry already installs it; it also force-appends LOW_QUALITY_TRANSACTION_PATTERNS to `ignoreSpans`.
- No middleware spans are emitted on Cloudflare — the transaction's `spans[]` under static lifecycle contains only the db/http.client children, no `middleware.hono` entries. I did not check whether that is intentional on CF vs. Node.
- The Cloudflare Vite plugin is safe alongside the Hono middleware, but I set `autoInstrumentation: false` deliberately so the plugin would not apply a second `withSentry` on top of the middleware's. I did not test whether leaving it at the default `true` double-instruments; that is a worthwhile follow-up probe.
- `mysql@2` connects to MariaDB on 127.0.0.1:3307 from inside workerd fine under `nodejs_compat` with a module-scope connection, in both the plain and the Vite build; only the span differs.
- Environment friction: ports 41337, 47213 and 47212-adjacent were already taken by sibling agents mid-run; I moved to 47211 / 47212 / 53871. Two wrangler starts had to be retried for that reason only.
- Stack frames arrive without `context_line` (hasContextLine false) in both builds. Expected for a dev run with no sourcemap upload, not a defect.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: An error thrown in `app.get("/error")` reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`, `handled:false`, stack frames with context lines, `sdk: sentry.javascript.hono`, and `transaction: "GET /error"`. Hono itself swallows it into a 500 response (curl saw 500, no crash), but the middleware's `responseHandler` reads `context.error` so nothing is lost; the server span is marked `internal_error`. Same in both lifecycles.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: `/users/:id` produced `GET /users/:id` with `transaction_info.source: "route"` and `http.route: "/users/:id"` in static lifecycle, and in the default stream lifecycle the `http.server` span carried name `GET /users/:id`, `sentry.segment.name.source: route` and `http.route: /users/:id`. This is the Hono middleware overriding the method-only name that `@sentry/deno`'s `Deno.serve` instrumentation would otherwise give.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent requests to `/tag/alpha|beta|gamma`, each doing `Sentry.setTag` then a 60ms await then `captureException`, produced three events with exactly one tag each (`reqtag: alpha|beta|gamma`) and three distinct trace ids; each event's trace id matches its own transaction's trace id. setup:
Koa runs on bun unchanged. Full Sentry wiring, which is what a docs page would have to show:

1. Install: `npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bun-10.67.0.tgz ... koa @koa/router mysql` (here: node_modules/@sentry/{bun,core,node,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry} symlinked to $W/packages/*, koa/@koa/router/mysql symlinked from the worktree).

2. `instrument.ts`:
```ts
import * as Sentry from '@sentry/bun';
Sentry.init({ dsn: '...', tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:52734/', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' /* or default 'stream' */ });
```

3. `app.ts` starts with `import './instrument';` as the very first line, then Koa + @koa/router, and a MODULE-SCOPE `mysql.createConnection({host:'127.0.0.1',port:3307,user:'root',database:'app'})`.

4. A Bun plugin build is mandatory (this is the whole story for Koa on Bun), `build.ts`:
```ts
import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin';
await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', external: ['@sentry/*'], sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });
```

5. Run: `bun run build.ts && bun dist/app.js`.

`Sentry.setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` (which the Koa/Node guide tells you to call) is NOT needed here, the bundled koaIntegration captures handler errors on its own with mechanism `auto.middleware.koa`.

Without the plugin build (`bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` or `bun app.ts`), Koa is completely uninstrumented: no router span, no db span, url-sourced transaction names, and handler errors are never captured at all.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: With the plugin build, `throw new Error('koa boom')` inside a router handler arrives as an event with mechanism `auto.middleware.koa`, handled:false, contextlines present, and the enclosing transaction gets status `internal_error`. Koa does not swallow it from Sentry's view, it also prints its own stderr trace and returns HTTP 500. No `Sentry.setupKoaErrorHandler(app)` call was made. Without the plugin build the same request produces only a transaction with status internal_error and NO event: the error is lost.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: With the plugin build the segment is `GET /users/:id` with source `route` (static: `transaction_info.source=route`; stream: `sentry.segment.name.source=route`, `http.route=/users/:id`), plus a child `router /users/:id` span (op `router`, origin `auto.http.koa`). Without the plugin build it degrades to `GET /users/42` with source `url` and no child span.

capabilities.name: isolation

capabilities.name: incoming trace

notes:
Two findings worth carrying forward.

1. The unbundled Koa-on-Bun failure is worse than the established "no library spans" note (toolbox: Bun records NO library spans for Express/Koa/Hapi/Fastify). Route names silently degrade to url source AND the thrown handler error never reaches Sentry at all. Koa's default `ctx.onerror` writes to stderr and answers 500, and with no koaIntegration patch in place there is nothing between Koa and the http server subscription that turns the 500 into an event. The practical consequence: a user following the Bun guide verbatim gets transactions and logs and believes the setup works, while every route error is dropped. The SDK emits no warning unless `debug: true`.

2. Contradiction with the docs Alert at bun/index.mdx:96-100. The claim that auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code is exactly inverted for the Bun plugin path: `sentryBunPlugin()` inside `Bun.build` is what makes auto-instrumentation work. The Alert is presumably about generic bundlers, but as written it steers Bun users away from the only working setup.

Other observations:
- `mechanism: auto.middleware.koa`, `sentry.origin: auto.http.koa`, span op `router` with `koa.name` / `koa.type` / `http.route` attributes.
- Module-scope mysql connection was used, per K11. Not re-derived: I did not test a request-scope connection.
- Low-cardinality naming from the recent commits is visible in stream mode: `http.client | GET 127.0.0.1` and `db | SELECT users`, while static mode still shows the descriptive `GET http://127.0.0.1:52740/downstream` / `SELECT id, name FROM users`.
- Ports used: 52732 (bare check), 52734 (sink), 52740 (recorder), 52742/52744 (app). All processes killed and all five ports verified free before returning. node_modules under the probe dir are symlinks only (dir total 2.3M, mostly dist/app.js + sourcemap), so nothing was deleted.

framework: Koa 3.2.1 + @koa/router (plain node:http server behind cloudflare:node httpServerHandler), @sentry/cloudflare 10.67.0 from develop
runtime: Cloudflare Workers (wrangler 4.129.0 dev / workerd 1.20260903.1, compatibility_date 2026-05-01, compatibility_flags nodejs_compat + enable_nodejs_http_server_modules)

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: Koa swallows the error by default: with no `app.on('error')` handler, a `throw` in `router.get('/boom/:id')` returns 500 and the server span gets `status: "error"`, but NO event ever reaches Sentry. Adding `app.on('error', err => Sentry.captureException(err, {mechanism:{type:'koa.onerror',handled:false}}))` (Koa's own idiom) makes it arrive, with sdk `sentry.javascript.cloudflare`, full request data (url/method/headers), and the same trace id as the request span, so the manual capture is correctly scoped to the request. There is no automatic mechanism, so the mechanism type is whatever the user writes. `hasContextLine` is false. Same under stream and static lifecycle; under static the transaction gets `status: "internal_error"`.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: No route name at all. @koa/router is not instrumented on Cloudflare, and the Worker-level `HttpServer` integration never sees the matched route. Stream lifecycle: `GET /users/42` produces a segment named just `GET` with `sentry.segment.name.source = "url"` and no `http.route` attribute. Static lifecycle: `transaction: "GET /users/42"`, `source: "url"` - the raw path, so high cardinality. Manual naming does work from inside a Koa handler: `Sentry.updateSpanName(Sentry.getRootSpan(Sentry.getActiveSpan()), `${ctx.method} ${ctx._matchedRoute}`)` yields `GET /named/:id` with source `custom` in both lifecycles. That `Sentry.getActiveSpan()` returns the request span inside the Koa handler also proves the AsyncLocalStorage context survives the httpServerHandler -> node:http bridge.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent `GET /tag/{alpha,beta,gamma}` requests, each doing `Sentry.setTag('reqtag', t)`, then an async sleep of 30-90ms, then `captureException`. Each event carried exactly its own tag and a distinct trace id that matched its own request span (alpha 45f08af3..., beta 6c7d0af5..., gamma 11046bde...). No cross-talk. withSentry's per-request isolation scope reaches through into the Koa middleware chain. Stream lifecycle.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: `GET /users/99` with `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus a matching baggage header produced a segment span with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. Stream lifecycle.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:41337/rec')` from inside a Koa handler produced an `http.client` child span with `origin: auto.http.fetch` (stream: `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`, parent = the server segment; static: the transaction's `spans` contains `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41337/rec`). The local recorder saw both propagation headers: `sentry-trace: ad8f621d61c04419a70a413f4c9a6c77-83d9c7bf8af874b9-1` and a full `baggage` with trace_id/sampled/sample_rate.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: The query itself works: a MODULE-SCOPE `mysql.createConnection({host:'127.0.0.1',port:3307,user:'root',database:'app'})` queried from a handler returned real MariaDB rows (`{"rows":[{"id":1,"name":"ada"},{"id":2,"name":"linus"}]}`) under plain `wrangler dev`, but emitted zero db spans (static lifecycle transaction `GET /db` came back with `"spans": []`). The only instrumentation path on Cloudflare is the Cloudflare Vite plugin's `buildTimeInstrumentation`, and it is fatal here: `vite build` with `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({autoInstrumentation:false})` does inject the channel (the bundle contains `orchestrion:mysql:query` twice, and grows 987kB -> 2.99MB) but workerd then refuses to start the worker with `Uncaught Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope`. Bisected: bare Koa through Vite + @cloudflare/vite-plugin boots; + `@sentry/cloudflare` and `withSentry` (no Sentry Vite plugin) boots; + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({autoInstrumentation:false})` fails; + `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({autoInstrumentation:false, buildTimeInstrumentation:false})` boots again. So `buildTimeInstrumentation: true` (the default) is what breaks a node:http/httpServerHandler worker, independent of mysql (the mysql-free variant fails identically) and independent of `ssr.noExternal`. mysql2's own diagnostics channels are not an escape hatch: `mysql2-dc-subscriber` exists in @sentry/server-utils but is not in @sentry/cloudflare's default integration list (observed `sentry.sdk.integrations`: Dedupe, EventFilters, FunctionToString, ConversationId, LinkedErrors, Fetch, HttpServer, RequestData, Console, SpanStreaming).

capabilities.name: logs

capabilities.name: client errors
capabilities.detail: No browser surface: this is a server-only Koa app on workerd, there is no client bundle and no @sentry/browser in play.

Two findings that are not about a single capability:

1. `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` with its default `buildTimeInstrumentation: true` makes a node:http/`httpServerHandler` worker fail to start on workerd ("Disallowed operation called within global scope"). Bisected across four builds; it is not mysql-specific and not `ssr.noExternal`-specific. This removes the only db-span path on Cloudflare for any framework of this shape (Koa, Express, Fastify behind httpServerHandler), so db spans here are broken rather than merely absent.

2. Installing the develop tarballs partially is a trap. `npm install sentry-cloudflare.tgz sentry-core.tgz` alone makes npm resolve `@sentry/server-utils` and `@sentry/opentelemetry` from the registry at the same 10.67.0 version, and the resulting mix fails the wrangler esbuild step with `Could not resolve "@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels"` and six missing `@sentry/core` exports.
