setup:
Koa runs on Deno, and the base Deno SDK works with it, but ONLY with the Deno import hook OFF. Wiring a docs page would have to show:

1) package.json + `npm install koa @koa/router mysql $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{deno,core,server-utils,server-runtime-injection}-10.67.0.tgz`
2) deno.json:
   { "nodeModulesDir": "manual",
     "imports": { "@sentry/deno": "npm:@sentry/deno", "koa": "npm:koa", "@koa/router": "npm:@koa/router", "mysql": "npm:mysql" } }
3) instrument.ts (must be evaluated before the Koa app module):
   import * as Sentry from "@sentry/deno";
   Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" });
4) main.ts: `import "./instrument.ts"; import "./app.ts";`  -- NO `import "@sentry/deno/import";`
5) Because the Koa integration cannot attach its own error handler, the app must register one by hand:
   app.on("error", err => Sentry.captureException(err, { mechanism: { type: "manual.koa.onerror", handled: false } }));
   (@sentry/deno does not export `setupKoaErrorHandler`; @sentry/node and @sentry/bun do. `attachKoaErrorHandler` is exported from @sentry/server-utils but is not a documented user API.)
6) Run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`

Adding `import "@sentry/deno/import";` (the documented way to get library instrumentation on Deno) makes the process die at import time before the server ever listens. There is therefore no configuration in which Koa spans, Koa's auto error handler, or db spans are available on Deno.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: Koa swallows the route error into its own `app.onerror` default logger; with the SDK wired the standard way (no hook) NO event reaches Sentry for GET /boom, only a transaction with status internal_error. The Koa integration's auto error handler (attachKoaErrorHandler, driven by the `orchestrion:koa:callback` channel) never fires because the channel is only injected by the import hook, which crashes Koa. A hand-written `app.on('error', e => Sentry.captureException(e, {mechanism:{type:'manual.koa.onerror',handled:false}}))` does work and produces a correctly scoped event (right trace_id, transaction 'GET /boom'). @sentry/deno exports no `setupKoaErrorHandler`, unlike @sentry/node and @sentry/bun. traceLifecycle static and stream both.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: No route name at all. Under traceLifecycle 'static' the server transaction is named from the raw URL: name 'GET /users/42', source 'url'. Under the default 'stream' lifecycle the server span is just 'GET' with no `http.route` and no `sentry.source` attribute. The parameterized name '/users/:id' never appears because the Koa router instrumentation (which is what sets http.route via setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute) requires the import hook. Spans come from denoHttpIntegration (node:http), not from Koa.

notes:
Headline: Koa itself runs fine on Deno, and the base @sentry/deno SDK gives useful telemetry alongside it, but the Deno import hook and Koa are mutually exclusive. `import "@sentry/deno/import";` kills the process at import time on `statuses/index.js` -> `require('./codes.json')` (denoland/deno#36240, the same root cause as the known `generator-function/require.mjs` failure, but a different file on koa@3.2.1 — koa@3 dropped generator-function, so the first `require('*.json')` in its graph is `statuses`). I also confirmed this is NOT scoped to a local node_modules: with `nodeModulesDir: "none"` the same crash happens inside Deno's global npm cache copy of statuses.

Consequences that a docs page would have to state plainly:
1. Zero Koa spans on Deno. No middleware span, no router span, no `http.route`, no `sentry.source: route`. Server spans come from denoHttpIntegration only and are named from the raw URL (static) or just `GET` (stream).
2. Zero automatic error capture on Deno. Koa swallows handler errors into `app.on('error')`; the SDK's auto-attach runs off the `orchestrion:koa:callback` channel, which the hook injects, so it never fires. Users must register `app.on('error', ...)` themselves. @sentry/deno does not re-export `setupKoaErrorHandler` (deprecated but present on @sentry/node, @sentry/bun, astro, aws-serverless, elysia, gcp-serverless, remix, solidstart, sveltekit). The internal helper is reachable as `import { attachKoaErrorHandler } from '@sentry/server-utils'` but that is not a user-facing API.
3. `debug: true` is actively misleading here: it prints "[instrumentation:koa] subscribing to channels" and "Integration installed: Koa" with no hook loaded and nothing instrumented. Same for Mysql/Mysql2. A user reading the debug log would conclude Koa is instrumented.
4. Deno fetch (K2) reproduces inside Koa: no span, no propagation headers. `node:http` client calls from the same handler do get an http.client span with sentry-trace and baggage, so that is the only working outgoing-propagation path.
5. Side observation from the hook sanity check (main-hook-nokoa.ts, no Koa involved): the mysql span from a module-scope pool arrives as its OWN root transaction with a different trace_id than the enclosing http.server transaction, i.e. db spans on Deno are not parented to the request even when the hook works. Worth a separate cell.

notes:
NestJS runs on Bun cleanly, and the Sentry story splits sharply on whether you bundle.

- Unbundled (`bun src/main.ts`, the shape a user copies from the Nest docs) you get errors with the right nestjs mechanism, isolation, trace continuation, outgoing fetch spans with headers, and logs, but URL-named transactions (`GET /users/42`, source `url`) and no middleware, handler or db spans. Nothing warns about this unless `debug: true` is set. This matches the known Bun finding that library spans need the plugin build.
- Bundled with `sentryBunPlugin()` everything lands: `GET /users/:id` source `route`, express middleware/handler children, and the mysql span. The one Nest-specific gotcha is that Bun's bundler statically resolves Nest's `loadPackage()` requires, so `@nestjs/microservices`, `@nestjs/websockets`, `class-validator`, `class-transformer`, `cache-manager` must be listed in `external` or the build fails; keeping `@sentry/*` bundled (as the task hint says) worked and is required for the plugin's injected channels to line up.
- The route name comes from the express layer, not from Nest: there are no Nest-specific spans (no `Controller.method` / nestjs interceptor spans) in either lifecycle. `SentryModule.forRoot()` was imported as the docs prescribe but contributed no visible spans on Bun; the only thing that demonstrably mattered from @sentry/nestjs was SentryGlobalFilter.
- SentryGlobalFilter is load-bearing: remove the APP_FILTER provider and Nest's built-in exception layer swallows the throw completely (transaction with internal_error, zero events). A docs page for this combination must not present it as optional.
- Static vs stream: route naming, db and http.client spans, isolation and trace continuation were verified in BOTH lifecycles and agreed. Static was used for the tag/trace-id assertions because tags and nested spans[] are easier to read there; stream additionally showed the low-cardinality names (`db SELECT users`, `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`).
- All five processes were killed and node_modules (131M) removed. Ports used: 53101 (sink) and 53102-53105 (apps); 47311/47312 were already taken by other agents.

Adding a global `@Catch()` filter extending BaseExceptionFilter that calls Sentry.captureException produces the event with mechanism "generic", handled true, correct trace_id, and full request context (url/method/headers, user.ip_address). No automatic mechanism exists: @sentry/cloudflare's httpServerIntegration never sees the throw because Nest converts it to a 500 response inside the node:http server. traceLifecycle 'static'.

notes:
Headline: NestJS + @nestjs/platform-express DOES run on workerd, and with the right build it is one of the better-instrumented Cloudflare framework cells (parameterized route names, middleware/handler/db/http.client spans) - but every bit of that depends on undocumented build wiring, and a plain `throw` in a controller still never reaches Sentry.

Findings worth filing:
1. `@sentry/server-utils/orchestrion/esbuild` is the missing documented path for non-Vite Cloudflare bundles. Enabling it flips route names from `GET /users/7` / source url to `GET /users/:id` / source route and adds the db span. @sentry/cloudflare's baseSdk.js:27-33 explicitly says only the Vite plugin injects the channels; the esbuild plugin exists and works, but no docs page mentions it.
2. With that plugin enabled, a Worker that calls `NestFactory.create` at module scope fails to BOOT: "Disallowed operation called within global scope ... generating random values are not allowed within global scope" originating in @nestjs/common/services/console-logger.service.js. The identical source without the plugin boots fine. So the orchestrion esbuild transform changes when the Nest module graph is evaluated (eager instead of lazy through esbuild's __require wrappers). Workaround: boot Nest lazily inside the fetch handler with dynamic imports. This is a real trap and would need to be in any docs page.
3. Errors are silently lost by default. Nest's ExceptionsHandler turns the throw into a 500 inside the node:http server, so @sentry/cloudflare's httpServerIntegration only sees a 500 response and records `status: internal_error` with no event. There is no `@sentry/nestjs`-style SentryGlobalFilter usable here (@sentry/nestjs pulls in @sentry/node), so the user must hand-write a `@Catch()` filter. A docs page must say this or users will think error monitoring is on when it is not.
4. workerd's `createRequire` cannot resolve `node:`-prefixed builtins ("No such module \"node:process\""), while `await import('node:process')` works (verified with app/probe/probe.mjs: {"hasGlobalProcess":"object","nodeProcess":"object","nodeNet":"function"}). Any esbuild-bundled CJS dependency that does `require('node:x')` - mysql2 does - needs a banner shim that strips the prefix. Even then `node:process` specifically must be aliased to a module returning globalThis.process.
5. mysql2 is unusable on workerd: `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. Use `mysql@2`. Worth stating in the Cloudflare guide's database section.
6. Packaging trap that cost a build cycle: installing only sentry-cloudflare + sentry-core tarballs makes npm pull the RELEASED @sentry/server-utils@10.67.0 from the registry, which has no `./no-diagnostic-channels` export, and wrangler then fails with "Could not resolve \"@sentry/server-utils/no-diagnostic-channels\"" x6. The develop tarball must be installed alongside. This is a real hazard for anyone on a mixed install, not only for this harness.
7. Two TS diagnostics that do not block emit but look wrong: `cloudflare:node` has no type declarations shipped anywhere reachable, and `sendDefaultPii: true` fails with "Type 'true' is not assignable to type 'never'" against @sentry/cloudflare's option type - worth a look at the CloudflareOptions type.

All results above came from traceLifecycle: 'static'. I did not run a 'stream' pass; with stream the transaction envelopes become span envelopes and the same names should apply, but that is untested here.

3. `instrument.ts` — the workaround line is mandatory, without it the app cannot boot:
   (globalThis as Record<string, unknown>).__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { runtimeUnavailable: true };
   import * as Sentry from "@sentry/nestjs";
   Sentry.init({ dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: "static" });
   The assignment must be evaluated before Sentry.init() (ESM hoisting is fine: the hook registration happens inside init(), not at module evaluation).

4. `main.ts`: `import "./instrument.ts";` as the first line, then `import "reflect-metadata";`, then Nest. Register BOTH pieces from @sentry/nestjs/setup:
   @Module({ imports: [SentryModule.forRoot()], controllers: [...], providers: [{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }] })
   SentryModule.forRoot() alone registers only APP_INTERCEPTOR; without the explicit APP_FILTER every route-handler error is swallowed and no event is sent.

5. Run: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`

Why the workaround: Sentry.init() -> registerDiagnosticsChannelInjection() calls `Module.registerHooks({resolve,load})` because hasStableSyncModuleHooks() returns `true` unconditionally when globalThis.Deno is set (node_modules/@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/register.js:10-15 and :55-57). In Deno 2.9.0 ANY Module.registerHooks() call breaks `require('*.json')`. I isolated it with a no-op hook and no Sentry at all (probe try-hooks-noop.mts vs try-hooks-none.mts), so it is a Deno bug (same family as K3 / denoland/deno#36240), but the develop SDK walks straight into it on Deno.

notes:
Headline: NestJS runs fine on Deno, and @sentry/nestjs (i.e. @sentry/node) initializes fine on Deno — but the develop SDK's default runtime injection makes the combination unbootable, and the fix is a one-line global that no docs page mentions and that is not a supported public option.

1. Root cause, worth a real fix. `hasStableSyncModuleHooks()` in `packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts` (built copy: node_modules/@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/register.js:10-15) returns `true` for Deno unconditionally, so init() always calls `Module.registerHooks({resolve, load})`. Deno 2.9.0 then compiles every `require('*.json')` as JavaScript and throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`. I proved this is Deno's bug with a no-op hook and zero Sentry code, but the SDK is the thing that triggers it, and the blast radius is large: express, statuses, fastify, mysql2, i.e. every Nest HTTP adapter. Two candidate fixes: gate the Deno branch behind a version check the way the Node branch is gated, or expose a documented opt-out (today the only lever is the undocumented `globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION__ = { runtimeUnavailable: true }` sentinel).

2. Second papercut. `SentryModule.forRoot()` registers only `APP_INTERCEPTOR` (setup.js:128,139); there is no `APP_FILTER`. My first run had forRoot() and nothing else and every route-handler throw was silently swallowed: 500 to the client, internal_error transaction, zero events. Adding `{ provide: APP_FILTER, useClass: SentryGlobalFilter }` fixed it immediately. Any Deno page would have to spell that out.

3. Pleasant surprise worth writing down: db spans need no instrumentation path at all on this stack. mysql2 3.24.3 publishes its own node:diagnostics_channel events (lib/tracing.js) and @sentry/node subscribes eagerly on Bun/Deno, so the query spans arrive with the injection hook explicitly disabled. Drivers without native channels would still be dark here, and there is no working escape hatch for them on Deno since the injection hook cannot be enabled.

4. `[Sentry] @sentry/server-runtime-injection was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... load uninstrumented` fires on Deno in the default (injection-on) run even though nothing is bundled. Misleading message on this runtime.

5. Deprecation noise: Deno 2.9 prints `Warning experimentalDecorators compiler option is deprecated and may be removed at any time` on every run. NestJS 10 still needs it, so a docs page cannot avoid the warning.

6. traceLifecycle made no difference to any verdict. Static was easier to read (nested spans[] on the transaction); stream confirmed the same trace ids, parents, tags and db spans, with server spans named "GET" and the db span low-cardinality "SELECT users".

7. Not probed, out of scope for this cell: @sentry/deno was installed but never used — the Node SDK is what @sentry/nestjs pulls, and mixing in @sentry/deno would give a second client. Profiling, cron/@SentryCron, and GraphQL/microservice transports were not exercised.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: A throw in an app-router route handler reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.function.nextjs.route_handler`, `handled: false`, sdk `sentry.javascript.nextjs@10.67.0`. The framework does not swallow it: the response is 500 and the enclosing transaction is `internal_error`. Only gap is `hasContextLine: false`, since this is a production build with source maps disabled. From traceLifecycle 'static' and confirmed again under 'stream'.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: Parameterized route is named `GET /app/api/users/[id]` with `transaction_info.source: "route"` (static lifecycle) and as an `http.server` span of the same name under stream lifecycle. Correct low cardinality, but the name carries a spurious `/app` prefix from the app-router directory, and the same request's event payload disagrees: `event.transaction` is `GET /api/users/[id]` while the transaction envelope says `GET /app/api/users/[id]`, so events and transactions group under different names.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent `GET /api/iso?tag=alpha|bravo|charlie`, each doing `Sentry.setTag` then a 150ms await then `captureException`. Each event carried exactly one tag, its own, and a distinct trace id matching its own transaction. No cross-talk, so bun's AsyncLocalStorage backs the isolation scope correctly under Next.js. traceLifecycle 'static'.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request with `sentry-trace: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1234567890abcdef-1` plus a matching baggage header produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111` and `parent_span_id: 1234567890abcdef`. traceLifecycle 'static'.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: `fetch()` from inside a route handler to a local recorder produced NO `http.client` span, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: null, baggage: null`. The NodeFetch integration installs (`Integration installed: NodeFetch`) but @sentry/node instruments undici's diagnostics channels; bun's `fetch` is native and emits none. Distributed tracing is silently severed at every outgoing call. Broken under both 'static' and 'stream'. This differs from plain `@sentry/bun`, where fetch spans and headers do work; the Next.js path pulls @sentry/node instead.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: A module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool queried from a route handler produced no `db` span; the transaction contained only Next's own three spans. Both instrumentation paths fail. (a) Runtime hook: `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` - `@sentry/nextjs/build/import-hook.mjs` no-ops on bun, and stays unregistered whether launched plainly, with `NODE_OPTIONS="--import ..."` (bun ignores it), or with `bun --bun --preload ./node_modules/@sentry/nextjs/build/import-hook.mjs`. (b) Build-time injection: `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]`, because Next's server build leaves `mysql2` as a bare `require("mysql2/promise")` external; tested with and without `serverExternalPackages: ['mysql2']`, identical. The Bun.build + `sentryBunPlugin()` path that rescues plain Bun apps does not exist for Next.js, so no path works. The SDK does detect bun and subscribes eagerly (`[instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly`), so it silently believes it is instrumented. traceLifecycle 'static'.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: `Sentry.logger.info('M-nextjs-bun log from route handler', { probe: 'logs' })` inside a route handler arrived as a `log` envelope item: `info: M-nextjs-bun log from route handler`. Flushed within the 7s timer window. traceLifecycle 'static'.

notes:
Time-boxed to ~25 min for the scaffold; both scaffold blockers were resolved so no not-run was needed.

Two scaffold failures that looked like bun bugs but are not:
- `The "id" argument must be of type string. Received undefined` from `next build` is Next 15.5.4's verifyTypeScriptSetup resolving `typescript/lib/typescript.js` against a TypeScript 6 install whose exports map has no such subpath. Node 26 reproduces it identically (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED). Fix is `typescript@5.x`, and Next auto-installs the bad version when tsconfig.json is present.
- `Export named 'withSentryConfig' not found` is a develop API move, not bun. Node fails the same way.

Bun-specific behaviour actually observed:
- The SDK detects bun and takes its `Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly` branch for every diagnostics-channel instrumentation, then still reports `contexts.runtime.name: "node"` on the wire. `process.versions.bun` is available (1.4.0) and unread.
- `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` is the single line that explains the db-span gap, and it is only visible with `debug: true`. A user on bun gets a silently half-instrumented SDK: no db/library spans, no outgoing http.client spans, no outgoing trace headers, and no warning.
- Bun ignores `NODE_OPTIONS=--import`; `bun --bun --preload` loads the file but the hook still declines to register.

Overall shape: everything that rides on Next.js's own OpenTelemetry emission plus the Sentry scope machinery works (errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace, logs). Everything that needs module patching, whether at runtime or at build time, does not.

All processes killed (sink 69262, recorder 69264, next 82995). app/node_modules (440MB) and app/.next removed. Sources kept.

capabilities.detail: A throw inside an App Router route handler is captured with mechanism `auto.function.nextjs.route_handler`, handled:false, and the request still returns HTTP 500 - Next.js does not swallow it. Same under both lifecycles. Stack frames carry no `context_line` (hasContextLine:false) because the worker bundle ships no sources; sourcemaps were disabled in this probe.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: Parameterized route /api/users/42 produces transaction `GET /api/users/[id]` with `transaction_info.source: "route"` under traceLifecycle 'static', and root span `http.server GET /api/users/[id]` under 'stream'. No raw id leaks into the name.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent GET /api/iso?t=alpha|bravo|charlie, each doing Sentry.setTag + a 120ms await + captureException: every event carried exactly its own probe_tag and its own trace_id, and each transaction carried the matching tag and trace_id. No cross-talk (traceLifecycle 'static').

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request with `sentry-trace: aaaa...-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus baggage produced a transaction with trace_id `aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and parent_span_id `bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` (traceLifecycle 'static').

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: A `fetch()` from inside a route handler to a local recorder produced NO http.client span (the transaction's spans[] holds only the three Next.js internal spans) and the recorder received sentry-trace: null, baggage: null. Same with a `node:http` GET from the handler: request succeeds, no span, no headers. The NodeFetch integration installs but workerd's global fetch / node:http shim is not the undici instance it patches. Reproduced under both 'static' and 'stream'.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: mysql2 (module-scope pool) DOES produce db spans with no extra plugin or build step: `db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect`, `db SELECT id, name FROM users` ('static') / `db SELECT users` ('stream'). The path is mysql2's own built-in diagnostics_channel tracing (.open-next/server-functions/default/node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js publishes `mysql2:query`/`mysql2:connect`/`mysql2:pool:connect`), which @sentry/node subscribes to - no Vite plugin, no Bun plugin, no import hook. Two caveats: (a) the query itself always fails on workerd with `Code generation from strings disallowed for this context` because mysql2 builds row parsers with new Function, so you get spans but a 500; (b) the `mysql`@2 driver runs fine on workerd (rows returned) but produces NO spans at all, because it depends on require-in-the-middle patching which cannot work in the pre-bundled OpenNext worker. Related: at init the SDK logs `Failed to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks, so channel-based integrations will not record spans` / `TypeError: port1.on is not a function` - @sentry/server-runtime-injection cannot register on workerd.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: Sentry.logger.info inside a route handler arrives as a `log` envelope, `info: m-nextjs-cf log from route handler`, and its trace_id (76f656fe129a4489969d755035ea0f51) matches the enclosing transaction's.

The whole body of advice is two wrangler settings: nextjs.mdx:28-38 `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, and nextjs.mdx:40-54 `compatibility_date` >= "2025-08-16" "required to introduce https.request ... which the Sentry SDK needs to send data". nextjs.mdx:56 then says "You should start seeing error events, traces, and logs appear in Sentry." ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nextjs/best-practices/deploying-on-cloudflare.mdx:1-7 is a stub that only redirects to that page. Nothing else in docs/platforms/javascript/ or platform-includes/ mentions opennext/open-next.

What the page does not say, and my run shows it should: (a) the three setup traps above (withSentryConfig now only on @sentry/nextjs/config on the v11 line, the ESM next.config.mjs named-export failure, sendDefaultPii removed); (b) instrumentation.ts must sit in src/ when the app is in src/app, otherwise register() never runs and there is complete silence with no warning; (c) outgoing fetch and node:http from a handler get no client span and no trace headers, so distributed tracing out of a Cloudflare-hosted Next.js app is dead - the page's blanket "traces" claim overstates it; (d) @sentry/server-runtime-injection cannot register on workerd (`port1.on is not a function`) and the SDK prints a scary warning at every boot; (e) db instrumentation works only for libraries that publish their own diagnostics_channel (mysql2 does, mysql@2 does not) - and mysql2 itself cannot execute a query on workerd because of the codegen restriction. Note also that the page never mentions @sentry/cloudflare; @sentry/nextjs alone is the correct and sufficient package, and the SDK does detect the environment (it sets contexts.runtime.name to "cloudflare" and tags the SDK metadata "nextjs,cloudflare").
notes:
Ports used: sink 41337, wrangler dev 41338. Both processes killed; node_modules removed.

Overall this combination is in good shape: 6 of 7 probed capabilities work, and the one broken capability (outgoing fetch) is the same workerd-vs-undici gap the plain Cloudflare SDK works around with its own fetch instrumentation - @sentry/nextjs running on OpenNext gets @sentry/node's NodeFetch integration instead, which patches an undici that is not there. That is the single highest-value fix or docs caveat for this cell.

Both trace lifecycles were exercised end to end. 'static' produced `transaction` envelopes with the Next.js internal spans nested (`resolve page components`, `executing api route (app) /<route>/route`, `start response`) plus the mysql2 db spans; 'stream' produced `span` envelopes with the root named `http.server GET /api/users/[id]`. Route naming, error capture, isolation, incoming-trace continuation and the missing fetch span behaved identically under both; the db span description is the only difference (`SELECT id, name FROM users` under static vs the low-cardinality `SELECT users` under stream).

Two incidental environment facts worth passing on: `npm install typescript` now installs TypeScript 7, which Next 15 rejects outright ("TypeScript 7 is not supported by this version of Next.js"), so pin typescript@5. And this npm blocks postinstall scripts (workerd, esbuild) - harmless here because the platform-specific optional packages @cloudflare/workerd-darwin-arm64 and @esbuild/darwin-arm64 are installed directly.

Not probed (out of scope for this cell): browser/client-side errors and replay, middleware, server components / server actions, pages router, Durable Objects, and source map upload (sourcemaps were explicitly disabled). The build did warn that no `global-error.js` is present, which is the documented app-router requirement for React render errors.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: `throw new Error('boom-route-handler')` in an App-Router route handler reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with mechanism `auto.function.nextjs.route_handler`, `handled: false`, sdk `sentry.javascript.nextjs`, correctly linked to the `GET /api/error` transaction (same trace_id, parent_span_id set). The framework does not swallow it; the transaction is marked `internal_error`. Two caveats: `hasContextLine` is false (no source context on the frames), and `contexts.runtime` reports `{name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` — the Node SDK's Context integration reads `process.versions.node`, so a Deno-hosted Next.js app is indistinguishable from Node in Sentry. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: Parameterized route `/users/42` produces transaction name `GET /users/[id]` with `transaction_info.source = "route"` under traceLifecycle 'static', and span `http.server GET /users/[id]` under 'stream'. Nested Next.js spans (`resolve page components`, `executing api route (app) /users/[id]/route`, `start response`) all appear but carry no `sentry.op` (they serialize as op `undefined`/`?`).

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent `GET /api/iso?tag={alpha,bravo,charlie}` (each `Sentry.setTag` then a randomized 150-350ms await then `captureException`) produced three events and three transactions, each carrying only its own `probe_tag` and its own trace id, with the event's trace id matching its own transaction's. No cross-talk. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: `curl -H 'sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1' -H 'baggage: sentry-trace_id=aaaa…,sentry-environment=probe,…'` produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. Continuation happens in the `node:http` server instrumentation, which works on Deno. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: A `fetch()` from inside a route handler to a local recorder produced NO `http.client` span (the `GET /api/fetch` transaction contains only the three Next.js spans) and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: null, baggage: null`. Identical under traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'. This is the known Deno K2 gap (Deno's global `fetch` is not `node:http`-backed and the SDK's NodeFetch/undici instrumentation never sees it), and it is not fixed by Next.js' own fetch patching. Distributed tracing out of a Next.js-on-Deno server is therefore dead.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: `mysql2` (module-scope `createPool`) DOES produce `db mysql2.pool.connect`, `db mysql2.connect`, `db SELECT id, name FROM users` — but only because mysql2 v3.24 ships its own native `diagnostics_channel` tracing channels (node_modules/mysql2/lib/tracing.js:19-31), which the Sentry channel integrations subscribe to eagerly on Bun/Deno. `mysql@2` (module-scope `createConnection`), which has no native channels and depends on injection, produced NO span at all in the same build. So: no instrumentation path is available. The runtime path (`Module.registerHooks`) is exactly what has to be disabled to make the app boot; there is no Deno import hook for the Node SDK (`@sentry/deno/import` is a different SDK); and `withSentryConfig`'s `buildTimeInstrumentation` (default true) only injects `require("@sentry/nextjs/orchestrion-runtime/register")` into the server chunks — it does not transform externalized `node_modules` deps, and that register call is itself the crashing one. Debug output confirms: `[Sentry] No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans.` traceLifecycle: 'static' and 'stream' both.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: `Sentry.logger.info('probe-log-from-route-handler', { where: 'nextjs-deno' })` inside a route handler arrived as a `log` envelope item `info: probe-log-from-route-handler`. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: client errors
capabilities.detail: Only the server runtime was probed. The browser bundle is produced by Next.js/webpack and served to a normal browser, so it is unaffected by the Deno host; nothing Deno-specific to test, and no browser driver was wired up in this cell.

notes:
Headline: Next.js on Deno is viable and the Sentry SDK is fully functional there, but the SDK as shipped bricks the app. A user following the Next.js docs verbatim on Deno gets a 100%-500 server with no indication that Sentry is the cause — the only clue is `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':' at Object.compileFunction (ext:core/01_core.js)`, which names neither Sentry nor JSON. The fix is one undocumented option, `enableRuntimeChannelInjection: false`. Two candidate SDK changes: (a) skip the `Module.registerHooks` branch on Deno, or feature-test it by attempting a JSON require before committing to it, since the resulting instrumentation is nearly worthless on Deno anyway; (b) at minimum, document the option in the Deno and Next.js guides. `hasStableSyncModuleHooks()` (packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:20-23) currently returns `true` for Deno unconditionally with the comment "The minimum supported Deno (2.8.3) always has stable sync module hooks" — the hooks are stable, but registering them is destructive on Deno.

Second finding, independent of Deno: `[instrumentation] failed to inject diagnostics-channel into mysql2: [TypeError: transform is not a function]` plus the always-on `@sentry/server-runtime-injection was bundled into your application` warning fire in a stock Next.js build. Next.js/webpack inlines `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` into `.next/server/`, tree-shaking the vendored meriyah transformer. This is the failure the warning was written for, and it happens on the default Next.js path — worth checking on plain Node too, it is probably not Deno-specific.

Third: `contexts.runtime` says `{name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` for a Deno-hosted app, because the Node SDK's Context integration reads `process.versions.node`. There is no way to tell from a Sentry event that the app ran on Deno. If Deno hosting is to be supported at all, this needs a `globalThis.Deno` check.

Fourth: `hasContextLine: false` on every exception event — the ContextLines integration reads no source lines under Deno + Next.js dist output.

Environment gotcha that cost me two probe rounds and is worth passing to other agents: ports 41213 and 47311 were already held by other agents' `sink.mjs` instances, which answer `{}` to every request. That looks exactly like a broken Next.js build (all routes returning `{}`, no Sentry envelopes) rather than a port collision. Always `lsof -nP -iTCP:$P -sTCP:LISTEN` before binding.

Cleanup: all six background processes killed (`server-opt`, `sink2`, `recorder`, and earlier servers); `node_modules` removed (418M reclaimed). `.next/` (173M) is left in place because the toolbox permits `rm` only on `node_modules`.

    compatibilityDate: '2025-07-15',

This boots and reports errors and logs, but produces ZERO spans and breaks trace isolation (see capabilities).

Two things that page gets wrong for this runtime:
- Its warning block (limited-server-tracing.mdx:19) claims top-level-import can only instrument native
  Node APIs and "will not capture data from database calls, queues, ORMs, third-party libraries". My node
  control run with exactly that setting produced `db SELECT users`, `db mysql2.pool.connect` and
  `http.client` spans, so on develop the restriction is weaker than documented.
- Nothing warns that on a non-node runtime the same setting silently degrades to errors+logs only, with a
  single process-wide trace id. There is no page telling a bun user to import `@sentry/bun` in

notes:
Headline: Nuxt itself runs fine on bun via `NITRO_PRESET=bun`, and @sentry/nuxt installs and boots, but the SDK a docs page would tell you to init (`@sentry/nuxt`, i.e. @sentry/node under the hood) is effectively tracing-blind on bun. Swapping one import in `sentry.server.config.ts` to `@sentry/bun` recovers server spans, route names, trace continuation, request isolation, outgoing-fetch propagation and db spans. That one-line difference is the whole finding.

Why the documented path degrades: the nitro `bun` preset serves through `Bun.serve`, not `node:http`. @sentry/node's HTTP server instrumentation never fires, so (a) no `http.server` span exists, (b) `setHttpServerSpanRouteAttribute` is a documented no-op without an active span so route names go nowhere, and (c) nothing resets the propagation context per request. `@sentry/nuxt`'s `patchEventHandler` (packages/nuxt/src/runtime/utils/patchEventHandler.ts) clones the isolation scope but never calls `setPropagationContext`, so on bun every event in the process lifetime shares the trace id minted at scope creation. Separately, `sentryCaptureErrorHook` (packages/nuxt/src/runtime/hooks/captureErrorHook.ts:48) writes the transaction name with `getCurrentScope().setTransactionName(...)`; with no per-request current-scope fork on bun that lands on the global scope and leaks the last-seen route onto unrelated events. Both are cheap to fix in the Nuxt runtime and would help every non-node nitro preset, not just bun.

Also logged on the bun run: `[Sentry] Runtime hook not registered` (node prints "registered"), which is the visible symptom of the module-hook layer being unavailable.

Orchestrion: the Nuxt module wires `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` into the nitro rollup config and force-inlines every instrumented package, yet the built `.output/server/index.mjs` contains no injected channels on EITHER preset (`[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]`, zero `orchestrion:` strings). Build-time instrumentation appears to be a no-op in the Nitro rollup pipeline. It happens not to matter for mysql2, because mysql2 v3 ships its own `diagnostics_channel` tracingChannels that @sentry/bun subscribes to eagerly, but any library that relies on orchestrion injection would get nothing here. Worth a separate look — one suspicious detail is that `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` spreads `codeTransformerRollup(...)` and then overrides its `options`/`buildStart` hooks.

Unrelated blocker worth recording for whoever reruns this: `@sentry/bundler-plugins` is not in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack and the registry's 10.67.0 is incompatible with develop's core — `nuxt build` fails at module import with `nodeStackLineParser is not a function` until you pack it from the worktree. I added it to $REPRO/_toolbox/pack.

Third-party bug, not ours: a `mysql2` query inside a nitro bundle always throws `genFunc$1 is not a function` (rollup commonjs interop on mysql2's `generate-function` dependency). Reproduced identically on the node-server preset under plain node, so it is not bun-specific and not Sentry-caused. Sentry still emits the db span, with the failure recorded as `error.type: TypeError` on it. I could not observe a *successful* db query in a Nuxt build because of this; the span shape is confirmed, the success path is not.

The one soft spot is route naming for non-parameterized server routes: `updateRouteBeforeResponse` (`packages/nuxt/src/runtime/hooks/updateRouteBeforeResponse.ts:17-40`) only sets the route attribute when `matchedRoute.path !== event.path`, so `/api/db` never gets `http.route` and, under the develop default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'`, its segment is the method-only `http.server GET`. Under `static` the same route still reads `GET /api/db` with `source: "url"`, so the gap is only visible on the streaming default develop now ships. Setting the route attribute whenever `matchedRoutePath` exists and is not `/**` would fix it.

The `--import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs` flow the Nuxt docs recommend has no Deno equivalent (`deno run` has no `--import`), so `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` is the only viable install method here, and it carries the documented "only native Node APIs are instrumented" restriction.

capabilities.detail: An error thrown in a nitro route handler is captured and is not swallowed: `/api/error` returns HTTP 500 and an `event` envelope arrives with exception `nuxt-deno-boom`, mechanism `chained`, sdk `sentry.javascript.nuxt`, and a source context line. Mechanism is the Nuxt module's h3 layer (nitro `error` hook / captureErrorHook plus the `patchEventHandler` proxy on `nitroApp.h3App.handler`), not the Node http instrumentation. Lifecycle: static (same under stream). Side note: `contexts.runtime` is reported as `{name: node, version: v26.3.0}` (Deno's node-compat version), so events are indistinguishable from real Node.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: No `transaction` and no `span` envelope is ever emitted for an incoming request, at either lifecycle. `getActiveSpan()` inside a handler is undefined (`/api/trace` returns `{"name":null}`), because nitro's deno_server preset serves through `Deno.serve` and the Node SDK only instruments `node:http`. The only route information that survives is the scope transaction name on the error event, and it is the raw URL: an error in `/api/users/[id].get.ts` produces `"transaction":"GET /api/users/boom"`, never `/api/users/:id`. `@sentry/nuxt`'s `updateRouteBeforeResponse` hook bails out at `getActiveSpan()`, so the parameterized name and the `url.path.parameter.*` attributes are never applied. Source cannot be reported since there is no transaction envelope.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent `/api/tag?tag=alpha|beta|gamma` requests each set a distinct tag and captured a distinct error. All three events carried `"tags":{"probe_tag":"gamma"}` and all three carried the same trace id `8991806e4d9246c2bde0ae1409ebc746`, which was also the trace id of unrelated requests minutes earlier and of the later sentinel. Root cause is visible in the debug log: `patchEventHandler` only clones when the current isolation scope is the default one, so request 1 logs `Created new isolation scope` and every later request logs `Using existing isolation scope` and shares it. A leaked `transaction` field confirms it (a sentinel captured after an unrelated request carried `"transaction":"GET /api/error"`). Lifecycle: static.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request to `/api/error` carrying `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a matching baggage header produced an event with `"traceId":"8991806e4d9246c2bde0ae1409ebc746"` (the process-wide id) and no `parent_span_id`. Headers are never read because nothing wraps the `Deno.serve` request, and the h3 patch only forks the isolation scope, it does not call `continueTrace`. Lifecycle: static.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: A `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:30412/rec')` from inside `/api/fetchout` completed normally but produced no `http.client` span (no span or transaction envelope at all) and the recorder saw no propagation headers: `[{"url":"/rec","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null},{"url":"/rec","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null}]`. Same as the already-known Deno finding K2, and it holds through the Nuxt/nitro build too. Lifecycle: static.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: No instrumentation path exists for this combination: there is no Bun plugin, no Deno import hook (the app is a rolled-up nitro bundle, not a node_modules import graph), and no Cloudflare Vite plugin. The SDK's own build-time injection ran and injected nothing: `[Sentry] Bundler plugin ran, injected libraries=[]` and `[Sentry] Runtime hook registered, injected libraries=[]`. Separately, a module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool cannot even execute in the deno_server output: `/api/db` returns 500 with `genFunc$1 is not a function` (the `generate-function` dependency broken by nitro's rollup bundling for the deno preset). That second failure is a Nuxt/Deno packaging bug, not a Sentry one, but it means no db span is reachable either way. Lifecycle: static.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: `Sentry.logger.info('hello-from-nuxt-deno', { where: 'handler' })` inside `/api/log` arrives as a log envelope: `{"type":"log","items":["info: hello-from-nuxt-deno"]}`, after the usual ~7s flush timer. Lifecycle: static.

docsNote: No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Nuxt on Deno. `grep -rni deno docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/` returns nothing, and `grep -rni "nuxt|nitro" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/` returns nothing; the Deno guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx, 232 lines) covers only plain `Deno.serve`/`Deno.cron`. The two Nuxt install pages that a user would land on both assume a Node process and both mislead here: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/cli-import.mdx:33 prescribes `node --import ./.output/server/sentry.server.config.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` (there is no `--import` on `deno run`), and cli-import.mdx:42 only says "Make sure to update the paths accordingly, especially when using a different Nitro preset". docs/platforms/javascript/guides/nuxt/install/limited-server-tracing.mdx:38 claims the SDK "will then automatically import this file at the top of the Nitro server entry file in the build output" - with the deno_server preset it does not (see notes). limited-server-tracing.mdx:18 does warn that only native Node APIs are instrumented under this method, which is consistent with what I measured, but it does not warn that request isolation and trace continuation are lost on a runtime whose server is not `node:http`.
notes:
Bottom line: Nuxt 4 builds and runs fine on Deno with the `deno_server` preset, and @sentry/nuxt gives you errors and logs there, but everything that depends on a server span (route names, isolation, incoming trace, outgoing propagation, db spans) is dead, and the wiring the docs describe does not work unmodified.

SDK bugs found (both in @sentry/nuxt 10.67.0 on develop):

1. `autoInjectServerSentry: 'top-level-import'` writes to the wrong file with any non-node preset.
   `addSentryTopImport` (node_modules/@sentry/nuxt/build/module/module.mjs:170-176) derives the entry
   filename from `nitro.options.commands.preview` via
   `getFilenameFromNodeStartCommand` = `/[^/\\]+\.[^/\\]+$/` (module.mjs:52-56). For deno_server the
   preview command is `deno task --config .output/deno.json start`, so the regex yields the literal
   string `deno.json start`. The module then creates `.output/server/deno.json start` containing
   `import './sentry.server.config.mjs';\nundefined` (readFile of a nonexistent path -> `data` is
   undefined, and the error is never surfaced because the callback ignores `err`). The real entry
   `.output/server/index.mjs` is left untouched, so Sentry never initializes and the failure is
   completely silent even with `debug: true` (the success log fires regardless). Same trap applies to
   any preset whose preview command is not `node <file>.mjs`.
   Worth fixing twice over: (a) resolve the entry from `nitro.options.rollupConfig.output.entryFileNames`
   first rather than from the preview command string, and (b) check `err` in the readFile callback.

2. Request isolation collapses on any runtime without node:http server instrumentation.
   `patchEventHandler` (runtime/utils/patchEventHandler.js) clones the isolation scope only when
   `getIsolationScope() === getDefaultIsolationScope()`. On Node the http instrumentation has already
   forked per request so reusing it is right; on Deno nothing forks, request 1 installs a clone and
   every later request sees that clone as "existing" and reuses it forever. Tags, transaction names and
   the propagation context (hence the trace id) are then process-global. A `Deno.serve`-shaped runtime
   needs the h3 patch to fork unconditionally and to `continueTrace` from the incoming headers.

Other observations:
- `contexts.runtime` reports `{name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` on Deno 2.9.0, so events give no hint
  the app is on Deno.
- Manual `Sentry.startSpan` works and produces a proper `transaction` envelope with nested `spans[]`,
  so the transport and tracing core are fine; only the automatic server span is missing.
- `traceLifecycle: 'static'` was used for every result above. Under the default `'stream'` the picture
  is the same (no span envelopes for requests).
- Nuxt/nitro bug unrelated to Sentry: a module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool throws
  `genFunc$1 is not a function` at query time in the deno_server bundle (the `generate-function`
  dependency is inlined by rollup and breaks). mysql2 is therefore unusable on this preset regardless
  of instrumentation.
- Nuxt/tooling gotcha that cost time: `npx nuxt build --buildDir X` moves the output to `X/.output`,
  flips the preview command back to `node`, and drops the api route chunks; always build with the
  default buildDir when testing this combination.
- Ports 41338/41339 were occupied by another agent's sink partway through, which silently swallowed one
  round of envelopes; all reported results were re-collected on 30411/30412/30413-30415.
- All processes started were killed; `node_modules` was removed (275 MB freed). Rerun with RERUN.sh.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: Bun.serve(app.fetch), no middleware: the handler throw is captured automatically with mechanism `auto.http.bun.serve`, handled:false, hasContextLine true, sdk sentry.javascript.bun, and the request span goes status=error; Oak does not swallow it (it logs "[uncaught application error]" and re-throws out of app.fetch). With an optional try/catch middleware the event instead carries mechanism `oak` handled:false and dedupeIntegration keeps only one. Stream and static lifecycle both. Under app.listen() the error NEVER reaches Sentry unless a manual middleware captures it, and the manual capture then lands on a stale process-level trace id.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: Out of the box the span is `http.server GET` with sentry.segment.name.source = url (stream) / transaction `GET` (static): Bun.serve names the span before Oak has matched anything, and Oak's fetch mount gives Bun.serve no `routes:{}` map. A 6-line ROUTER-level middleware reading ctx.matched.at(-1).path plus updateSpanName + SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE='route' produces `http.server GET /users/:id` src=route (stream) and `GET /users/:id` source=route (static). Because it is router middleware and runs before the handler, it also names the error path: static gave `GET /error` source=route status=internal_error, unlike the Deno cell where the after-next() middleware missed it. Under app.listen() the middleware is a silent no-op (getActiveSpan() is undefined for all 9 requests).

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Bun.serve(app.fetch), stream lifecycle: three concurrent GET /iso/:tag requests (each setTag('who', tag), 60-120ms await, setTag('who2', tag), captureException) produced three events with exactly their own tags {who: X, who2: X} and three distinct trace ids, each equal to its own http.server span trace id. Under app.listen() this is broken exactly as on Deno: all three events carried who=charlie and one shared stale trace id a2cdf2f5080346759b636800a82cb887.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request carrying sentry-trace + baggage continues the trace before Oak is involved (the Bun.serve wrapper runs continueTrace). Stream: `http.server GET /users/:id` with trace_id aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa and parent_span_id 1111111111111111. Static: transaction `GET /ok` trace cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc parent 3333333333333333. This is the one capability that also works under app.listen() (trace bbbb... parent 2222222222222222), because it is read in the Bun.serve callback, not in the handler.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: fetch() from inside an Oak handler to a local recorder produced `http.client GET 127.0.0.1` (origin auto.http.fetch) as a child of the request segment on the same trace id, and the recorder saw both headers: sentry-trace 0b22b3d098774f229c80398d8f002378-899c8c8d7d6377f8-1 and a full baggage with sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fdownstream. Static lifecycle nests it as `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41402/rec/from-oak` inside the `GET /downstream` transaction. No Deno-style K2 gap on Bun. Under app.listen() the client span still fires and still carries headers, but as its own root segment on the process-level trace, disconnected from the request.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: Module-scope mysql2 connection queried in the handler: stream gives `db SELECT users` with parent_span_id = the request segment and the same trace id, origin auto.db.mysql2.diagnostic_channel, db.query.text 'SELECT id, name FROM users', db.system mysql; static nests `db SELECT id, name FROM users` inside the `GET /db` transaction. Instrumentation path: NONE was needed - plain `bun app.ts`, no Bun.build/sentryBunPlugin bundle, because mysql2 publishes its own diagnostics_channel events that the SDK subscribes to. (A driver without native diagnostics_channel support would still need the sentryBunPlugin bundle per the Bun baseline.) Under app.listen() the db span disappears entirely - it is not emitted at all, not even as a detached root.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: Sentry.logger.info('hello from oak', { route: '/log' }) inside a handler arrived as a log envelope correlated to the request: `info: hello from oak :: trace=865f3beb418f416dacf9e2abd9300128`, the same trace id as the `http.server GET /log` span. Stream lifecycle, Bun.serve mount. Under app.listen() the log arrives but is stamped with the stale process trace (a2cdf2f5...) instead of the request's.

capabilities.name: client errors
capabilities.detail: Oak is a server-only framework with no browser surface; this probe ran server-side on Bun only.

notes:
Headline: Oak on Bun is the best Oak result so far, and the whole story fits on one docs page, but only if the page says three things.

1. Mount shape. `Bun.serve({ fetch: req => app.fetch(req) })` gives everything: auto error capture, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, nested db and http.client spans, correlated logs. `app.listen()` silently loses errors (zero events without a manual capture), loses the db span entirely, detaches the fetch client span onto a process-level root trace, stamps logs with that stale trace, and leaks isolation scopes across concurrent requests (all three concurrent events carried who=charlie and one shared trace id). Root cause is the same as the Deno cell: Oak's own server drains requests through an async queue, so the handler body escapes the AsyncLocalStorage context the Bun.serve wrapper opened. Note the span origin under app.listen() is still `auto.http.bun.serve`, i.e. Oak's listen() path does use Bun.serve internally on Bun - the SDK sees the request, it is only the handler body that escapes the context. This is one SDK issue shared across Deno and Bun and probably every framework with its own accept loop.

2. Route names are not automatic, and the middleware placement matters more than on Deno. Registering the naming middleware on the ROUTER (`router.use`) rather than the application makes it run before the handler with ctx.matched already populated, so it also names the error path - `GET /error` came back source=route status=internal_error, which the Deno cell's after-next() variant could not do. `updateSpanName` alone stamps source `custom`; the explicit `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE='route'` attribute is what produces src=route.

3. Install. Oak ships on JSR only. `bun add @oak/oak` fails; the working line is an `.npmrc` with `@jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io` plus `npm install "@oak/oak@npm:@jsr/oak__oak@17.2.0"`. Any Oak-on-Bun page has to lead with that.

- The Bun baseline "no library spans without a bundle" is not universal. mysql2 produced a correctly parented `db SELECT users` span under plain `bun app.ts` with no Bun.build and no sentryBunPlugin, because mysql2 publishes its own diagnostics_channel events. The bundle is needed for drivers/frameworks the SDK has to patch, not for ones that self-publish. The docs alert at bun/index.mdx:98 telling users bundling breaks auto-instrumentation is also stale relative to sentryBunPlugin.
- Outgoing fetch works fully on Bun (span + sentry-trace + baggage), so the Deno K2 gap is Deno-only; an Oak page for Bun needs no workaround section there.

Error middleware is optional on the Bun.serve path and should be presented that way: without it the error still arrives as `auto.http.bun.serve` handled:false because Oak re-throws after logging "[uncaught application error]". A user who registers an Oak `error` event listener would stop that re-throw and then does need the manual capture.

Packaging is the real story here. Oak's current line (17.x) ships only to JSR; the npm package @oakserver/oak is stuck at 14.1.0. Any docs page must show the `@jsr:registry=https://npm.jsr.io` .npmrc line plus the `npm:@jsr/oak__oak` alias, otherwise a user following it installs a three-major-versions-old Oak.

Oak needs zero adaptation for Workers: Application.fetch is documented in Oak's own source as a Cloudflare fetch handler and takes (request, env, ctx). Everything @sentry/cloudflare provides at the withSentry layer therefore works unchanged, which is why six of seven capabilities are green with no Sentry-side Oak support at all.

The one real gap is route names. Because Sentry only sees the Worker fetch boundary, a parameterized Oak route is reported as the raw URL (static lifecycle) or as bare "GET" (stream lifecycle). Oak exposes matched layers on ctx.matched, so an ~8-line middleware fixes it, but two things make that workaround imperfect and worth an SDK-side fix or at least a documented snippet: setting the sentry.source attribute after updateSpanName is honoured in stream lifecycle (source "route") but not in static lifecycle (source stays "custom"); and the middleware runs after `await next()`, so on a throwing route it never executes and the error transaction keeps the unparameterized name.

A second reportable wart: a request that throws out of the handler still produces a server transaction/span with status "ok", even though the error event is captured and the response is a 500.

The db result contradicts the assumption that Cloudflare db spans need the Vite plugin's buildTimeInstrumentation. The vite build with a bare sentryCloudflareVitePlugin() also succeeded (1495 modules, ~4MB worker) and produced identical spans, so the plugin is optional here.

Separately, mysql2 cannot actually execute a query on workerd: it compiles row parsers with `new Function`, which workerd rejects with `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`. Sentry still reports the span (status error). Any Cloudflare + MySQL guidance should point at mysql@2, not mysql2.

notes:
Headline: Oak is fine on Deno, but the mount shape decides whether the SDK works at all. `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` is the only shape worth documenting; `app.listen()` silently loses errors, route names and span parenting, and actively leaks isolation scopes between concurrent requests (a correctness bug a user would experience as wrong tags/users on events). Root cause: Oak's `listen()` server drains requests through its own async queue, so the handler body escapes the AsyncLocalStorage context that `wrapDenoRequestHandler` opened inside the Deno.serve callback. `Deno.serve(app.fetch)` keeps the handler inside that context. This is worth an SDK issue independent of docs — Oak's listen path is the same shape other Deno frameworks with their own accept loops will have.

Second gap: route names are not automatic. `denoServeIntegration` names the span before Oak has matched anything, so every request is `GET` (stream) or the raw URL (static). The 6-line `ctx.matched.at(-1).path` middleware in the setup field fixes it and is what a docs page must ship. Two caveats to document with it: it runs after `await next()`, so it never fires on the error path (the `/error` span keeps `src=url`), and it needs `SENTRY_SEGMENT_NAME_SOURCE = 'route'` explicitly because `updateSpanName` alone stamps source `custom`.

Third: Oak's `app.fetch` is typed as a Cloudflare fetch handler `(request, env, ctx)`. On Deno the second argument is `ServeHandlerInfo`, and Oak resolves the client IP only from the `CF-Connecting-IP` header, so `ctx.request.ip` is empty. Harmless for Sentry (the SDK reads the address from `info.remoteAddr` itself), but it will confuse anyone comparing `ctx.request.ip` with the `client.address` on the span.

Fourth: with `nodeModulesDir: "manual"` Oak does not boot until `path-to-regexp@^6.3.0` is present in node_modules — a hard blocker that any docs page pairing Oak with the symlinked/manual SDK setup has to call out. Also note `npm install` in that directory deletes sibling symlinks, so the `@sentry/*` links must be re-created after it.

Errors reaching Sentry twice (auto `auto.http.deno` from the Deno.serve wrapper plus a manual `oak` capture from the middleware) is currently masked by `dedupeIntegration`. Only one event arrived in every run. Docs should therefore present the error middleware as optional on the `app.fetch` path and required only if the user registers an Oak `error` listener (which would stop the re-throw).

Outgoing fetch is the known Deno K2 gap and reproduced unchanged here (no span, no headers); nothing Oak-specific. Client errors are not applicable — Oak is server-only.

4. `instrument.server.mjs`: `Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' })` from `@sentry/react-router`.
5. `server.js`: `import "./instrument.server.mjs";` as the very first line (Bun has no `--import` ESM loader), then the stock Express server, then `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler(app)`.
6. `vite.config.ts`: add `sentryReactRouter({ sourcemaps: { disable: true } }, config)` after `reactRouter()`.
7. Build with node (`npx react-router build`), run with `PORT=<port> bun server.js`.

That setup boots and serves 200s. It records errors and logs. It records NO spans of any kind and has NO request isolation — see capabilities.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: An error thrown in a `/users/:id` loader reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with `mechanism.type: "react-router"`, `handled: false`, stack frames with context lines, sdk `sentry.javascript.react-router`. React Router does not swallow it: it also lands in the app log and the request returns 500. The mechanism comes from `Sentry.createSentryHandleError` exported as `handleError` from entry.server; `Sentry.setupExpressErrorHandler` never sees it because React Router turns loader throws into a 500 response. The event carries NO `transaction`, no request context and no per-request trace id.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: No server transaction or span envelope is produced at all on Bun, in either lifecycle, so there is no name to inspect. The error event for `GET /users/1?mode=error` also has `transaction: undefined` — `wrapSentryHandleRequest`/`updateRootSpanWithRoute` both bail out because `getActiveSpan()` returns undefined. In the loader `Sentry.getActiveSpan()` is null on every request. Root cause: @sentry/node on develop logs `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` then `No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans.`; node:http is a builtin so neither the Vite/orchestrion plugin nor sentryBunPlugin can inject into it. Identical with traceLifecycle 'static' and 'stream'.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Badly broken, and the most serious finding. Three concurrent `/users/:id?mode=isolation&tag=...` requests (delays 300/150/50 ms) each called `Sentry.setTag` then `captureException`. All three events, plus a sentinel captured afterwards, carry `probe_tag: "charlie"` (last writer wins) and all four share one trace id `75b8f65c357d4cafa81856d25173c558`, the process-lifetime propagation context that stayed identical across every request in the run. There is no per-request isolation scope because there is no http server instrumentation to fork one, so tags from one user's request leak into every other user's events.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request to `/users/1?mode=error` carrying `sentry-trace: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` plus matching baggage produced an error event with `trace_id: 428283e35934487b92fff4b874cce656` (the process-wide id) and no `parent_span_id`. The incoming headers are never read, again because nothing instruments the incoming request.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: A `fetch()` from inside the loader to a local recorder produced no `http.client` span and no propagation headers. The recorder echoed exactly `{"connection":"keep-alive","user-agent":"Bun/1.4.0","accept":"*/*","host":"127.0.0.1:52817","accept-encoding":"gzip, deflate, br, zstd"}` — no sentry-trace, no baggage. The NodeFetch integration installs but does nothing on Bun. This differs from @sentry/bun, which does instrument fetch; @sentry/react-router pulls in @sentry/node instead.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: Module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool in `db.server.ts`, queried from the loader, returns rows but produces no db span. I tried both instrumentation paths. (a) Vite/orchestrion: `ssr: { noExternal: ["mysql2"] }` so sentryReactRouter's sentryOrchestrionPlugin transforms it — the injected channel names are verifiably in the bundle (`orchestrion:mysql2:execute`, `orchestrion:mysql2:query` in build/server/assets/context-*.js) and the SDK logs `[instrumentation:mysql2] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly / subscribing to channels`. Nothing fires. (b) Bun plugin build: `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ["./server.bun.js"], target: "bun", external: ["@sentry/*"], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` — this removes the `No diagnostics-channel injection detected` warning and injects `orchestrion:router:handle`/`orchestrion:router:register` into the bundled Express, yet still yields zero spans. Same on bun 1.3.14. Even with injection present no root span exists and no span is emitted.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: `Sentry.logger.info('probe log from loader', { id })` inside the loader arrives as a `log` envelope after the ~7s flush timer: `info: probe log from loader`. Its trace_id is the process-wide propagation-context id (`77a8afb086af461b90fa06d4ab8b864f`), not a per-request one, so logs from concurrent requests are not separable by trace.

capabilities.name: client errors
capabilities.detail: Out of scope for this cell: the browser half of @sentry/react-router runs in the viewer's browser and is unaffected by the server runtime being Bun. I probed only the server.

The React Router guide declares `categories: [javascript, browser, server, server-node]` (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx:5-9) and says at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/react-router/index.mdx:156 "The wizard also creates a server configuration file for Node.js runtime." The Bun guide (docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/index.mdx) names no frameworks at all. So the docs neither claim nor deny Bun support for React Router; a reader following either guide lands in the broken state described above.
notes:
What a docs page would have to say, if one existed:

1. The stock React Router node template does not run on Bun at all, Sentry aside. `react-dom/server` resolves to `server.bun.js`, which has no `renderToPipeableStream`. The user must rewrite `app/entry.server.tsx` around `renderToReadableStream`. That is a React Router/Bun issue, not a Sentry one, but it has a Sentry consequence: `Sentry.createSentryHandleRequest` takes `renderToPipeableStream` as a required option, so the canonical Sentry wiring (docs and the react-router-8-framework e2e app) is unusable on Bun. Only `Sentry.wrapSentryHandleRequest` works.

2. `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` is a runtime dependency of `@sentry/react-router` and is not in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack, so it must be packed from the worktree before anything installs. Worth flagging for whoever maintains the pack directory.

3. The substantive finding: on the develop (v11) line `@sentry/node` has dropped the OTel SDK and takes all of its instrumentation from diagnostics channels registered by `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` (its only remaining OTel dep is `@opentelemetry/api`). The registration API (module.registerHooks / the `--import` loader) does not exist on Bun, so the SDK logs `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` and node:http is never patched. With no `http.server` root span there is no request-scoped isolation scope, and that cascades into every other capability: no transactions, no route names, no trace continuation, no fetch propagation, no db spans, cross-request tag leakage, and one process-lifetime trace id shared by every event and log.

4. Build-time injection does not rescue it. I confirmed the Vite/orchestrion plugin really does inject `orchestrion:mysql2:query` into the bundled driver, and that `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` really does inject `orchestrion:router:handle` into the bundled Express and silences the `No diagnostics-channel injection detected` warning — and still no span is emitted, on bun 1.4.0 and on the CI pin 1.3.14. This is consistent with and extends the established K11 finding: on Bun the injected channels do not fire even for a module-scope driver loaded at startup. And because the missing root span comes from node:http, a builtin nothing can rewrite, no amount of bundling can fix the server side.

5. Practical consequence: React Router on Bun with @sentry/react-router today is an error-and-log-only SDK with a correctness hazard (tag and trace leakage across concurrent requests). Supporting the combination needs either a Bun-native http server instrumentation in @sentry/node (or a Bun.serve adapter like @sentry/bun's), or an explicit docs statement that the React Router server SDK requires Node.

6. `traceLifecycle` made no difference: I ran both 'static' and 'stream' and got zero span/transaction envelopes either way, so every result above is lifecycle-independent. Bun reports `process.version` as v26.3.0 (1.4.0) / v24.3.0 (1.3.14), and the SDK's `runtime` context plus its own `runtime: node` tag both say node, so events sent from Bun are indistinguishable from Node events in Sentry.

Cleanup: both processes killed (ports 52817/52818 confirmed free), app/node_modules removed; the probe directory is now 9.1 MB.

notes:
Scaffold notes worth carrying into a docs page:
- `future: { v8_viteEnvironmentApi: true }` in react-router.config.ts is mandatory for React Router 7.18 + @cloudflare/vite-plugin. Without it `vite build` dies with `[commonjs--resolver] id.endsWith is not a function` on both vite 6.4.3 and 7.3.6, because the ssr environment gets the client route inputs with `{index: 'virtual:cloudflare/worker-entry'}` pushed in as an object. The message names neither plugin and is very hard to attribute; this alone would sink most users.
- `@react-router/node` must be pinned to ^7 alongside react-router 7: @sentry/react-router's peer range `">=7.15.0 || ^8.x"` makes npm hoist 8.3.1 and the install aborts with ERESOLVE. Nothing in the app actually uses @react-router/node on Workers.
- `createSentryHandleError` is not exported from `@sentry/react-router/cloudflare` (packages/react-router/src/cloudflare/index.ts re-exports only `../client`, `wrapSentryHandleRequest`, `injectTraceMetaTags`). Errors thrown in loaders are silently swallowed into the ErrorBoundary until you write your own `handleError`. This is the single sharpest gap: the app "works", returns 500, and reports a transaction with status internal_error, so it looks instrumented while capturing nothing.
- `wrapSentryHandleRequest` calls `flushIfServerless` from `@sentry/core/server`; it bundles and runs fine in workerd.
- `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` bare is safe next to a manual `Sentry.withSentry()` in workers/app.ts (autoInstrumentation detects the already-wrapped entry), and its buildTimeInstrumentation is what makes db spans appear.
- Use `mysql` v2, not mysql2: mysql2 is instrumented (spans appear) but its query fails on workerd with `EvalError: Code generation from strings disallowed for this context`.
- The Cloudflare Vite plugin's dev server (`vite dev`) was not exercised; everything here ran against `vite build` output via `wrangler dev --config build/server/wrangler.json`.
- No SDK debug warnings of note; `debug: true` was on for all runs.
- Both `traceLifecycle: 'static'` and `'stream'` were run end to end and agreed on every capability. The stream run also confirms the new low-cardinality names (`GET 127.0.0.1` for http.client, `SELECT users` for db).
- Cleanup: all node/wrangler processes I started were killed and verified down (ports 47211, 47212, 52881, 52883 free); `node_modules` (398M) was removed, leaving 5.3M of sources and logs.

React Router framework mode runs on Deno, but NOT with the entry.server.tsx the docs show. Required wiring:

1. Packages (npm install, then run with deno):
   npm install react-router@^7 @react-router/dev@^7 @react-router/node@^7 react@^19 react-dom@^19 vite@^6 isbot@^5 mysql@^2
   npm install $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-router-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-node-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-core-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-server-runtime-injection-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-opentelemetry-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-react-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-browser-utils-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-replay-canvas-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-feedback-10.67.0.tgz $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-bundler-plugins-10.67.0.tgz

2. deno.json: { "nodeModulesDir": "manual" }

3. app/entry.server.tsx MUST use the web-stream renderer, not the node one. Deno resolves `react-dom/server` through react-dom's `deno` export condition, which points at the browser build and has no `renderToPipeableStream`. Use `renderToReadableStream` from `react-dom/server` and return `new Response(body, ...)`. Then wrap it:
     export default wrapSentryHandleRequest(handleRequest);
     export const handleError = createSentryHandleError({ logErrors: true });
   both from `@sentry/react-router`.

4. instrument.server.mjs (plain @sentry/react-router init; the `node` export condition resolves under Deno and every Node integration installs):
     import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react-router';
     Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel: 'http://127.0.0.1:<sink>/', tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' });

5. Server entry: a hand-written node:http adapter whose FIRST line is `import './instrument.server.mjs';`, then `createRequestHandler(build, 'production')` from `react-router` over `http.createServer`. The node:http server is what produces the http.server span and the isolation scope; a bare `Deno.serve` handler gets neither. `react-router-serve` and `NODE_OPTIONS='--import ./instrument.server.mjs'` (the two things the docs prescribe) are both unusable: Deno ignores NODE_OPTIONS, and react-router-serve goes through the renderToPipeableStream path Deno cannot load.

6. Build and run:
     npx react-router build
     PORT=<port> deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys server.mjs

7. Do not use mysql2 (see the db-spans finding). `mysql@2` works.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: A `throw new Error('rr-deno loader boom')` in a loader reaches Sentry as an unhandled event with `mechanism: "react-router"`, `handled: false`, sdk `sentry.javascript.react-router`, transaction `GET /boom`, and context lines. React Router swallows the throw into a 500 response, so the `createSentryHandleError({ logErrors: true })` export from entry.server.tsx is the mechanism that surfaces it; without that export nothing is reported. Static lifecycle; identical under stream.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: `GET /users/:id` with `source: "route"`, `op: "http.server"`, produced by `wrapSentryHandleRequest`. Same parameterized name under traceLifecycle 'static' (transaction envelope) and 'stream' (span envelope). One inconsistency: the error event's own `transaction` field carries the raw path (`GET /iso/alpha`) while the transaction/span carries `GET /iso/:tag`.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent GET /iso/:tag requests, each doing Sentry.setTag + a 120ms await + captureException. Each transaction and each event carried exactly its own `iso_tag` and its own trace id, no bleed. AsyncLocalStorage-backed isolation from the node:http server works under Deno. Static lifecycle.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request with `sentry-trace: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1234567890abcdef-1` plus baggage produced a transaction with that exact trace_id and `parent_span_id: "1234567890abcdef"`. Static lifecycle.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: Global `fetch` from a loader produces no http.client span and sends no sentry-trace/baggage: the recorder saw `{"url":"/rec-fetch","sentryTrace":null,"baggage":null}` and the enclosing transaction's spans[] was empty. This is Deno K2 (Deno's fetch does not emit the undici diagnostics channels NodeFetch hooks). `node:http` client from the same loader works fully: span `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:52103/rec-http` nested in the transaction with both headers set. Static lifecycle for the nested span; stream lifecycle showed the same client span as `http.client | GET 127.0.0.1`.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: No extra instrumentation path is needed: the SDK logs `[instrumentation:mysql] Bun/Deno, subscribing eagerly` and the diagnostics channel fires. But (a) `mysql2` cannot be loaded at all once Sentry is initialized: its `require('../package.json')` at connection_config.js:13 throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` through Sentry's runtime require hook (Deno's compileFunction; same class as K3 but triggered by @sentry/node's server-runtime-injection, not @sentry/deno/import). Plain Deno imports mysql2 fine. (b) With `mysql@2` a db span IS produced, but a MODULE-SCOPE pool detaches it from the request: the query arrives as its own root transaction `SELECT id, name FROM users` op `db` on a different trace id while `GET /db` has spans: []. A connection created inside the loader nests correctly: `GET /db` with spans `["db SELECT id FROM users"]`. This is the inverse of the Bun K11 rule. Static lifecycle.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: `Sentry.logger.info('rr-deno log from loader', { where: 'loader' })` in a loader arrived as a log envelope after ~7s carrying the request's trace id. Static lifecycle.

capabilities.name: client errors
capabilities.detail: Only the server side was probed. No browser was driven, so the @sentry/react-router client init, hydration and browser tracing were not exercised.
