notes:
Headline: React Router framework mode DOES run on Deno, and @sentry/react-router (the @sentry/node-based server SDK, resolved through the `node` export condition) initializes and installs every Node integration under Deno 2.9.0. Errors, parameterized route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation and logs all work. Three things do not.

1. The docs' entry.server.tsx cannot load on Deno. `react-dom/server` resolves through react-dom's `deno` export condition to the browser build, which has no `renderToPipeableStream`. Rewriting entry.server.tsx around `renderToReadableStream` fixes it and is the single change that makes this cell viable. It also rules out `react-router-serve`, which the docs' `start` script uses.

2. mysql2 is unusable. Once Sentry is initialized, `require('../package.json')` inside mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13 throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` in Deno's compileFunction. Same class as the established Deno K3 finding, but the trigger here is @sentry/node's own runtime require hook (server-runtime-injection), not @sentry/deno/import. Plain Deno imports mysql2 without complaint. A user following the React Router docs with mysql2 gets a hard crash at startup with no Sentry frame in the stack. `mysql@2` is unaffected.

3. Outgoing global fetch is invisible: no http.client span, no sentry-trace, no baggage. node:http client from the same loader works completely, pinning this on Deno's fetch not emitting the undici diagnostics channels (Deno K2, reconfirmed here through the framework SDK).

Secondary findings worth a line in any future docs page:
- A module-scope mysql pool detaches its db span from the request: the query lands as its own root transaction on a different trace id while the http.server transaction has empty spans[]. A connection created inside the loader nests correctly. This is the exact inverse of the Bun K11 rule, so a single cross-runtime docs sentence about connection placement would be wrong for one of them.
- Loaders and actions produce no spans of their own here. React Router 7.18 ships a server instrumentation API and @sentry/react-router exports `createSentryServerInstrumentation` for it, but there is no visible supported way to attach it to the ServerBuild (`unstable_instrumentation` is not on the ServerBuild interface in 7.18.3); not pursued inside the time-box. All transactions therefore have empty spans[] except where an http.client or db span landed.
- The SDK logs a misleading warning on Deno: "`@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... load uninstrumented. Keep `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` external in your server bundle". Nothing was bundled; mysql2 is external to the SSR build. The advice is unactionable on Deno.
- The error event's `transaction` field carries the raw path (`GET /iso/alpha`) while the transaction/span carries the parameterized name (`GET /iso/:tag`).
- Client-side (browser) behavior was not probed at all.
- Ports 41317 and 47311 were already held by other agents' recorders (they answered `{}` to every path), so probe a candidate port with curl before binding. Used 52101/52102/52103; all three processes killed and node_modules (158M) removed before returning.

  import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix';
  Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' });

server.mjs: `import './instrument.mjs';` as the FIRST line, then the standard express adapter
(`createRequestHandler({ build: await import('./build/server/index.js') })`). mysql2 pool created at
module scope in server.mjs.

app/entry.server.tsx: `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError;`

Build: `bun x remix vite:build` — works unmodified on Bun (vite 5 + esbuild darwin-arm64 binary).

Mode A (plain, what a Node docs page tells you to do):
  NODE_ENV=production bun server.mjs
  -> errors, isolation, incoming-trace continuation, trace headers on outgoing fetch, logs.
  -> ZERO transaction/span envelopes. No route names, no db spans, no http.client spans.

Mode B (Bun's documented instrumentation path — bundle with the orchestrion plugin):
  build-server.ts:
    import { sentryBunPlugin } from '@sentry/bun/plugin';
    await Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./server.mjs'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun',
      external: ['@sentry/remix','@sentry/node','@sentry/core','@sentry/bun','@sentry/server-utils',
                 '@sentry/opentelemetry','@sentry/server-runtime-injection'],
      plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] });
  then `bun build-server.ts && NODE_ENV=production bun dist/server.js`
  -> full span tree (route names, LOADER spans, mysql2 spans, http.client spans), errors, logs.
  -> request ISOLATION IS GONE: one trace id for the whole process, tags leak across requests,
     incoming sentry-trace ignored.

Root cause of the Mode B defect: @sentry/remix's per-request `withIsolationScope` + `continueTrace` live
in `instrumentServer()`, which monkeypatches `createRequestHandler` via a CJS
`loadModule('@remix-run/server-runtime', module)` (packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:538).
`sentryBunPlugin` force-un-externalizes every instrumented package (`withoutInstrumentedExternals` in
packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts) so `@remix-run/server-runtime` is inlined into the
bundle, and the monkeypatch lands on the unused node_modules copy. The plugin does not let you keep that
package external, so on Bun you can have spans or isolation, not both.

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: A loader throwing `new Error('probe-loader-boom-7')` reaches Sentry in BOTH Bun modes with `mechanism: auto.function.remix.server`, `handled: false`, `sdk: sentry.javascript.remix` — the framework does not swallow it, and the 500 still renders. Mechanism is the Remix `handleError` hook wired as `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError`. Plain `bun server.mjs` also gets `hasContextLine: true`; the Bun.build bundle loses it (`hasContextLine: false`) because the bundle is emitted without sourcemaps. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: Plain `bun server.mjs`: BROKEN — no transaction or span envelope is emitted at all for any request, so there is no name to read. With the `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` bundle: WORKS — `GET users/:id` with `source: route`, and the child loader span `function LOADER routes/users.$id`; the parameterized error route gives `GET boom/:id`. Identical to the Node control. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Plain `bun server.mjs`: WORKS — three concurrent /iso/{a,b,c} requests produced three events each carrying only its own `probe_tag` and its own trace id. With the `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` bundle: BROKEN — all three events carry `probe_tag: tag-c`, the tag leaks onto the later /sentinel event too, and every request in the whole process shares one trace id (510a3fcd98a14ddf9e60ae3a42f0c407 across 15+ requests). Cause: the plugin inlines @remix-run/server-runtime, defeating the CJS monkeypatch in instrumentServer.ts:538 that is the only thing calling `withIsolationScope`. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: Plain `bun server.mjs`: WORKS — a request with `sentry-trace: aaaa…-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` produced an event with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`, and the outgoing fetch re-emitted the upstream DSC (`sentry-environment=upstream`). With the Bun.build bundle: BROKEN — the same request is recorded under the process-global trace id 510a3fcd…, the upstream trace and DSC are discarded (`continueTrace` never runs, same root cause as isolation). traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: Plain `bun server.mjs`: headers only — the recorder received `sentry-trace: a19cc67a…-884e3f78b27078a5` and a baggage header, but NO `http.client` span was emitted (no span envelopes exist in this mode at all). With the Bun.build bundle: WORKS fully — transaction `GET outfetch` contains `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41519/rec`, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: 510a3fcd…-8f5c7bf3a115a44a-1` plus baggage with `sentry-transaction`, `sentry-sampled`, `sentry-sample_rate`. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions Remix on Bun. `grep -rniI "bun" ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/remix/` returns nothing; `grep -rniI "remix" ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` returns nothing (that guide is only index.mdx + configuration/). The single cross-hit in ~/dev/sentry-docs/platform-includes/ is a false positive on the word "bundler" in platform-includes/sourcemaps/troubleshooting/javascript.mdx:46.

What the Remix guide does say about the runtime is implicit: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/remix/index.mdx:9 tags the guide `server-node`, and index.mdx:12-16 carries only a "Remix 3 Not Yet Supported" alert — there is no runtime-support statement, no Bun caveat, and manual-setup.mdx has no `--import` / NODE_OPTIONS section at all (grep for `node --import|NODE_OPTIONS|import-hook` in manual-setup.mdx returns nothing).

So if a Bun page were written from what shipped, it would have to add two things that exist nowhere today: (1) that plain `bun server.mjs` yields no spans whatsoever, and (2) that the `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` workaround that restores spans simultaneously destroys per-request isolation and incoming-trace continuation.
notes:
Headline: Remix v2 itself is fully viable on Bun 1.4.0 — `bun x remix vite:build` and `bun server.mjs` both work unmodified, and @sentry/remix initializes. But there is no Bun run shape that gives a correct SDK, and the two shapes fail in opposite directions:

- Plain `bun server.mjs`: correct isolation, correct incoming-trace continuation, errors, logs, trace headers on outgoing fetch — and ZERO span/transaction envelopes. Consistent with the established Bun finding that `bun run` gets no orchestrion transform; here it also costs the `http.server` transaction entirely, because @sentry/remix disables @sentry/node's incoming request spans (`disableIncomingRequestSpans: true`, packages/remix/src/server/integrations/http.ts) and relies on the injected `@remix-run/server-runtime` channels for the request span.
- `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()`: complete span tree (route names with `source: route`, LOADER spans, mysql2 spans, http.client spans) — and request isolation is gone. Every request in the process shares one trace id, and tags set in one request are attached to every later event including unrelated ones. This is a data-correctness bug, not just a missing feature: it cross-contaminates events between concurrent users.

The isolation defect is structural, not a Bun runtime quirk. @sentry/remix's only per-request `withIsolationScope`/`continueTrace` lives in `instrumentServer()` (packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:349, :538), which reaches Remix by a CJS `loadModule('@remix-run/server-runtime', module)` monkeypatch. `sentryBunPlugin` calls `withoutInstrumentedExternals` (packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/bundler/bun.ts) to force-bundle every instrumented package, so `@remix-run/server-runtime` is inlined and the monkeypatch patches a dead node_modules copy. The plugin deliberately offers no escape hatch for this (its comment says a blanket external strategy is warned about, not supported), so the two mechanisms are mutually exclusive by construction. The same hazard would hit any bundled Remix server, Bun or not — Bun is just the runtime where bundling is mandatory.

Suggested fix direction for the SDK: move the isolation-scope fork and `continueTrace` off the CJS monkeypatch and onto the already-injected `orchestrion:@remix-run/server-runtime:requestHandler` tracing channel (packages/remix/src/server/integrations/tracing-channel.ts currently starts spans there but never touches the isolation scope), so bundled builds get isolation for free.

Node control, run from the identical source tree with `node --import ./node_modules/@sentry/remix/build/import-hook.mjs server.mjs`, is fully correct on every capability — so nothing here is a Remix-SDK-wide regression.

Two smaller observations: the Bun bundle drops `hasContextLine` (no sourcemaps configured in build-server.ts; adding `sourcemap: 'external'` would likely restore it, untested), and the Bun bundle is `target: 'bun'` so it cannot be run under node as a same-artifact control (`TypeError: __require is not a function`).

Environment: all processes started (sink 27419, recorder 41519, app 33851, node control 33853) were killed; app-a/node_modules removed. Ports 41317 and 52731 were occupied by other agents mid-run, hence the odd port numbers. `@sentry/remix` was installed from the pre-built $REPRO/_toolbox/pack tarball, so nothing needed packing from the worktree.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent requests each setting a distinct tag: all three events carried `probe_tag: bravo`, and so did a later unrelated /sentinel request. Trace ids were distinct, tags and request data were not. Cause is in the SDK, not Remix: `wrapRequestHandler` from @sentry/cloudflare/request is the only entry point that never calls setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy() (grep of packages/cloudflare/src: withSentry.ts:40, pages-plugin.ts:78, durableobject.ts:54, workflows.ts:247, instrumentWorkerEntrypoint.ts:153 all do), so withInvocationIsolationScope falls back to the stack strategy, which its own comment says degrades the fork to a no-op. Adding `SentryCF.setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy()` at module scope fixes it completely (each event then carries only its own tag, own URL and own trace id). Note the fix requires importing the @sentry/cloudflare main entry, which the Hydrogen docs page explicitly forbids on Oxygen. traceLifecycle: static.

notes:
Two SDK-side findings worth filing.

1) `wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request` has no request isolation. It is the only wrapper in packages/cloudflare/src that does not call `setAsyncLocalStorageAsyncContextStrategy()`, so `withInvocationIsolationScope` (packages/cloudflare/src/utils/invocationScope.ts) sees the stack strategy, `getIsolationScope() === getDefaultIsolationScope()` stays true and the fork is a no-op, exactly as its own comment predicts. Under concurrency every `setTag`/`setUser`/request-data write is global to the isolate and bleeds into unrelated later requests. This is the path the repo's own e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/remix-hydrogen/server.ts uses, and the path hydrogen-remix.mdx documents. Whether the fix belongs in `wrapRequestHandler` itself is a judgement call (the entry point exists to work without `nodejs_compat`, where AsyncLocalStorage is absent), but today neither the code nor the docs give the user any way to know isolation is off.

2) `makeWrappedCreateRequestHandler` from `@sentry/remix/cloudflare` double-reports on Cloudflare. Composed with `wrapRequestHandler` (the only sane way to get a client on Workers) it emits two `http.server` transactions per request in two different trace ids, because its `continueTrace` + `startSpan` (packages/remix/src/server/instrumentServer.ts:394-410) starts a fresh root instead of nesting under the Cloudflare root span; the outgoing-fetch headers then propagate the Remix trace and the Cloudflare transaction is orphaned. With an inbound sentry-trace header both roots share the incoming trace id, so the duplication is visible but the split is not. `instrumentBuild` alone avoids this entirely and still yields route-named transactions (its `updateSpanWithRoute` renames the enclosing Cloudflare root), so it is the shape to document, and the shape I ran the capability matrix on.

Smaller observations:
- With `instrumentBuild` alone the event's `transaction` field is unset (nothing calls `isolationScope.setTransactionName`); the transaction envelope is still named correctly. With the double-wrap the field is set. Minor grouping gap.
- Under Vite 6 a plain `vite build` builds only `build/client` and silently skips the Remix SSR build. `npx remix vite:build` is required. Anyone following a generic "run vite build" instruction gets a worker entry that imports a non-existent `build/server/index.js`.
- `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })` composes fine with the Remix Vite plugin without `@cloudflare/vite-plugin` present; only its build-time channel injection is used, and it needs `ssr.noExternal: true` so the driver is inside the Vite SSR bundle rather than left for wrangler's esbuild.
- npm needs `--legacy-peer-deps`: `@remix-run/cloudflare@2.17.5` peers `@cloudflare/workers-types@^4`, wrangler 4.129 peers `^5`.
- No dual-@sentry/core problem despite @sentry/remix being bundled by Vite and @sentry/cloudflare by wrangler: the `globalThis.__SENTRY__` carrier is shared, and a tag set through the Vite-bundled copy isolates correctly once the ALS strategy is installed by the wrangler-bundled copy.
- Probe routes are Remix resource routes (loader only, no component) so responses are JSON; the React render path was exercised only by `/` and the error boundary.
- All processes killed, `node_modules` removed.

setup:
Remix runs on Deno unchanged. Wiring that a docs page would have to show:

1. Install with npm under node (not `deno add`, not `bun add`), so the tarballs' transitive `@sentry/*@10.67.0` deps resolve:
   `npm install --legacy-peer-deps $REPRO/_toolbox/pack/sentry-{remix,node,core,react,browser,browser-utils,replay,replay-canvas,feedback,server-utils,server-runtime-injection,opentelemetry}-10.67.0.tgz '@remix-run/dev@^2.17.0' '@remix-run/node@^2.17.0' '@remix-run/react@^2.17.0' '@remix-run/server-runtime@^2.17.0' react react-dom vite@^5 mysql2 typescript`
2. `deno.json`: `{ "nodeModulesDir": "manual" }`.
3. `vite.config.ts`: `plugins: [remix(), sentryRemixVitePlugin()]` (from `@remix-run/dev` and `@sentry/remix`). The plugin runs at build time under node and prints `[Sentry Remix] Found 5 static and 3 dynamic routes`; the emitted route manifest is what makes parameterized transaction names work at runtime.
4. `app/entry.server.tsx`: `export const handleError = Sentry.sentryHandleError;`
5. `instrument.server.mjs`: `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/remix'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1.0, traceLifecycle: 'static' | 'stream' })`.
6. Server entry: `import './instrument.server.mjs'` first, then `createRequestHandler(Sentry.instrumentBuild(build), 'production')` over `node:http`. Do NOT use `@remix-run/express` / express on Deno — express dies at import on Deno via the known `require('*.json')` bug once the Sentry runtime hook is installed.
7. Build under node: `npx remix vite:build`. Run under Deno: `deno run --no-prompt --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys server.mjs`.

CAVEAT that must be in any such docs page: any CommonJS dependency that does `require('*.json')` (mysql2 does, `mysql2/lib/connection_config.js:13`) must be imported BEFORE `./instrument.server.mjs`, otherwise the process dies at startup. That inverts the usual "instrument first" rule.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: Works, but only with a non-canonical import order. mysql2 ships its own `diagnostics_channel` instrumentation (`mysql2/lib/tracing.js`), which the SDK subscribes to eagerly on Deno, so no instrumentation path is needed at all: no `@sentry/deno/import` hook, no esbuild/orchestrion plugin, no bundler plugin. With the canonical order (instrument first, driver after) the process dies at startup: `@sentry/server-runtime-injection`'s module hook makes Deno reject mysql2's `require('../package.json')` with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`, the same class as known finding K3. Findings worth flagging beyond the per-capability verdicts:

1. NEW: the "instrument first" ordering that every Sentry docs page teaches is actively harmful for Remix on Deno. `@sentry/server-runtime-injection`'s module hook makes Deno's CJS loader reject `require('*.json')` (`SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`), so any driver that reads its own package.json (mysql2 does) crashes the process at import if it is loaded after `Sentry.init`. This is the K3 bug reached through @sentry/node rather than through `@sentry/deno/import`. Deno bug denoland/deno#36240, but the SDK is what triggers it.

2. NEW: on Deno the SDK prints "`@sentry/server-runtime-injection` was bundled into your application, so mysql2 ... load uninstrumented" for an entry that is not bundled at all (plain .mjs, real node_modules). The advice in that warning is wrong for this runtime, and it appears immediately before the crash in 1., which will send users down the wrong path.

3. NEW: db spans need no instrumentation path on Deno. mysql2 ships native diagnostics_channel support (`mysql2/lib/tracing.js`) and the SDK's Bun/Deno "subscribing eagerly" branch picks it up, so neither the `@sentry/deno/import` hook nor an esbuild/orchestrion plugin is required. That also means the injection hook buys nothing for mysql2 on Deno while costing the crash in 1.

4. NEW: the obvious userland fix for the missing-fetch-span gap (wiring core's `addFetchInstrumentationHandler` + `instrumentFetchRequest` in a custom integration) propagates `sentry-trace`/`baggage` correctly but silently suppresses every server transaction/span for the whole process. Debug output shows the `http.server` root span is never finished. Worth an SDK issue on its own; it is the workaround a user would most plausibly reach for.

5. Confirms K2 (no fetch span, no trace headers on Deno) for the @sentry/node-based framework SDKs, not just @sentry/deno.

notes:
Root cause for the four broken capabilities is one thing: SolidStart 2's nitro output bundles srvx's **node** adapter (`.output/server/_libs/srvx.mjs` contains `node_modules/srvx/dist/adapters/node.mjs`), so the server is node:http-shaped, but @sentry/node's node:http server instrumentation has no effect under bun. Node emits three http.server spans per request (node:http outer + srvx + h3); bun emits only two (srvx + h3). The node:http layer is what forks the isolation scope and calls continueTrace, so on bun there is no per-request isolation, no per-request trace, and no trace continuation. @sentry/nitro's own srvx/h3 tracing channels do fire on bun (spans, parenting and nesting are all correct within a request) but they only start spans, they never fork isolation or continue a trace.

Second, independent bun gap: `module.registerHooks` is unavailable, so `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping` — the runtime path that instruments externalized deps like mysql2 is gone. The build-time replacement (`sentryOrchestrionPlugin` inside `sentrySolidStart()`) reported `injected libraries=[]` in every build I made, including one where I forced `ssr: { noExternal: ['mysql2'] }` and verified mysql2 really was inlined into `.output/server/_ssr/ssr.mjs`. So on this stack there is currently no working path to db spans on bun; a `@sentry/bun` plugin build is not applicable because the server is built by vite/nitro, not `Bun.build`.

Not bun-specific, and worth flagging separately for the SolidStart guide regardless of runtime: (a) a plain `throw` in a file API route is never reported — only server functions wrapped in `withServerActionInstrumentation` are; (b) transaction/span source is always `url`, never `route`, even for `/users/[id]`, which under the develop default `traceLifecycle: 'stream'` collapses the http.server span name to the bare method.

Also observed: `contexts.runtime.name` is reported as `node` when running under bun (bun sets process.versions.node), so bun-run events are indistinguishable from node-run events in Sentry.

Port hazard worth passing on: my first attempt used 41501/41502, both already held by another agent's node processes. Bun's srvx binds `[::]` while node binds `127.0.0.1`, so both listeners coexisted and every `curl 127.0.0.1` silently hit the *other* agent's server, producing plausible-looking wrong responses. Verify with `lsof -nP -iTCP:<port> -sTCP:LISTEN` before trusting any result.

@sentry/nitro's peer range (`>=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0 || 3.0.260311-beta || 3.0.260415-beta`) does not accept `nitro@3.0.260610-beta`, which is what the repo's own solidstart-2 e2e app pins; npm refuses without `--legacy-peer-deps`. That is a real install-time papercut for anyone following a docs page with npm.

capabilities.detail: Manual `Sentry.captureException` inside a route handler reaches Sentry (sdk `sentry.javascript.cloudflare`, mechanism `generic`, handled true), which also proves the external-Sentry/dedupe wiring works. But an error THROWN from a route handler never becomes an event: Nitro/h3 catches it, logs `[request error] [unhandled]` and returns a 500 Response, so `withSentry` only sees a 500 and marks the request transaction `internal_error`. The framework swallows it, and there is no SolidStart-side hook (no `@sentry/solidstart` server middleware) available on this runtime to re-raise it. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: `/api/users/42` produced transaction name `GET /api/users/42` with `source: "url"` — the raw path, not the `/api/users/:id` file-route pattern. `@sentry/cloudflare` has no knowledge of the Nitro/SolidStart router, and nothing parameterizes the name, so every distinct id is a distinct transaction name. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent GETs to /api/iso?who=alpha|beta|gamma (each with a 50-150ms random await between setTag and captureException) produced three events each carrying only its own `who` tag and its own trace id (a993566e…, dfc8c9a5…, dfd04c9a…), and the three request transactions carried the matching tag and trace id. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request with `sentry-trace: aaaa…aaaa-bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb-1` and a matching baggage header produced both the event and the request transaction with `trace_id: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa` and `parent_span_id: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb`. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: A `fetch()` from inside a route handler to a local recorder produced a child span `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:53819/rec` on the request transaction, and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: 17b563b8968242ddb69fd63b93baf171-a0929cbc2b0df026-1` plus a full baggage header whose trace_id matches the transaction. traceLifecycle: 'static'.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: mysql2 could not be loaded at all: a module-scope `mysql.createPool` in a route died on workerd with `TypeError: _3.hasOwnProperty is not a function` inside Nitro's rollup CJS interop shim (.output/server/chunks/_/promise.mjs), so no query ever ran. capabilities.name: logs

capabilities.name: client errors
capabilities.detail: With `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/solidstart` in `src/entry-client.tsx`, an unhandled `setTimeout` throw on the /clienterr route arrived as an event with `sdk: sentry.javascript.solidstart`, `mechanism: auto.browser.browserapierrors.setTimeout`, `handled: false`, plus a `pageload` transaction with browser/resource spans. The pageload trace id (4c6e507d…) is unrelated to the SSR request trace id, i.e. no server->client trace continuation, because nothing injects a sentry-trace meta tag into the SSR HTML on this path.

docsNote: No page in ~/dev/sentry-docs mentions SolidStart on Cloudflare. `grep -rn -i cloudflare docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/` returns nothing across index.mdx, install/{index,cli-import,dynamic-import,limited-server-tracing}.mdx, features/ and profiling/. In the other direction, `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` holds astro, hono, hydrogen-react-router, hydrogen-remix, nextjs, nuxt, remix, sveltekit and tanstack-start — there is no solidstart.mdx, and `grep -rn -i solidstart docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/` returns nothing. The nearest precedent is docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/nuxt.mdx:6, "This guide will show you how to set up the SDK with Nitro's `cloudflare_module` (or their deprecated `cloudflare-pages`) deployment preset." — the same Nitro preset family SolidStart uses, backed by packages/nuxt/src/runtime/plugins/sentry-cloudflare.server.ts:3 (`wrapRequestHandler` from `@sentry/cloudflare/request`). SolidStart has no such runtime plugin and no such page. docs/platforms/javascript/guides/solidstart/index.mdx:11 still flags the whole SolidStart SDK as beta.
notes:
Headline: SolidStart itself runs on Cloudflare Workers out of the box (`preset: 'cloudflare-module'` builds, and /, /api/* and file routes all serve correctly under wrangler dev), but `@sentry/solidstart` cannot: its server half is `@sentry/node` (packages/solidstart/src/server/sdk.ts:3) and it also pulls `@sentry/nitro`, so the documented `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/solidstart` in a server entry is unusable on workerd. Everything I measured came from hand-wiring `@sentry/cloudflare`'s `withSentry` around the Nitro output; a user following the current SolidStart docs gets nothing on the server.

Three concrete gaps a docs page or SDK change would have to close:
1. There is no `sentryCloudflareNitroPlugin` equivalent for SolidStart. Nuxt has exactly this (packages/nuxt/src/runtime/plugins/sentry-cloudflare.server.ts) and SolidStart is the same Nitro substrate, so the port looks mechanical.
2. The `rollupConfig: { external: ['@sentry/cloudflare'] }` step is non-obvious and silently fatal if you skip it: without it Nitro inlines a second `@sentry/cloudflare` into `.output/server/index.mjs`, so `Sentry.setTag` / `captureException` in a route handler run against an uninitialised client and produce nothing, while the request transactions from the wrapper still arrive and make it look like the SDK is working.
3. Nitro's cloudflare-module preset emits no wrangler config, so `main` has to point at a hand-written wrapper entry rather than at `.output/server/index.mjs`.

Two behaviours worth filing regardless of docs: thrown route errors are swallowed by Nitro/h3 before `withSentry` sees them (only a 500 and an `internal_error` transaction survive), and transaction names are raw URLs (`GET /api/users/42`, source `url`) because nothing feeds the SolidStart file-route pattern to `@sentry/cloudflare`. Both are exactly what a real SolidStart-on-Cloudflare integration would need to fix; both are already solved on the Node path by the SolidStart server middleware.

Also: no server-to-client trace continuation. The SSR HTML carries no sentry-trace meta tag, so the browser pageload starts a fresh trace.

Conversely docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-18 declares the Deno SDK (sentry.javascript.deno, beta) as a manual-setup server platform and names no framework anywhere in its 232 lines. So a user has nothing telling them that a SolidStart node-server build runs on Deno, nor that on Deno it loses outgoing-fetch tracing and leaks the first scope write.
notes:
Key surprise: this combination works far better than expected, because @sentry/solidstart on develop does build-time (orchestrion) instrumentation inside the vite build. The Deno runtime never has to patch modules, so mysql2 db spans work with no @sentry/deno import hook and no --import flag. The server SDK is @sentry/node (index.server.js re-exports it) and its OTel setup boots cleanly under deno 2.9.0.

Two Deno-specific defects, both confirmed against a node control run of the exact same .output bundle:
1. Outgoing fetch: no http.client span and no propagation headers (known Deno finding K2), while node produces both.
2. Scope leak: the first Sentry.setTag in the process sticks to the shared default isolation scope and shows up on every later request that does not overwrite it. Node does not leak. Worth an issue: it means one request's tags/user/context can be attributed to unrelated later requests on Deno.

Two framework-level gaps that are NOT Deno's fault (node behaves the same):
- A throw from an API route handler never becomes a Sentry event; only the transaction turns internal_error. Users must wrap handlers themselves (or use withServerActionInstrumentation for 'use server' functions, which is what the e2e app solidstart-2 does).
- Route names are not parameterized: static gives "GET /api/users/42" with source url; stream gives just "GET". Same shape as the Bun/Nitro catch-all finding — the transaction carries the raw URL rather than the route pattern, so the name is high cardinality in static and useless in stream.

Packaging friction worth a docs line: npm refuses the install without --legacy-peer-deps because @sentry/nitro's peer range does not accept nitro 3.0.260610-beta (the version @solidjs/start 2.0.2 pulls); pnpm, which the e2e app uses, is more lenient.

The name is the SvelteKit route id, not the URL. With kit tracing on, the enclosing kit root span is renamed and re-attributed by `sentryHandle`.

capabilities.name: isolation

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: A request with `sentry-trace: cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc-dddddddddddddddd-1` plus baggage produced a server span with `trace=cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc` and `parent=dddddddddddddddd`. Server-to-client continuation also works: the SSR HTML carries `<meta name="sentry-trace">` and `<meta name="baggage">`.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: A `fetch()` from inside `/api/out` to the local recorder produced NO `http.client` span and the recorder saw `sentry-trace: null, baggage: null`. Root cause is visible: `diagnosticsChannel.channel('undici:request:create').hasSubscribers` is `false` on bun and `true` on node for the identical build, so @sentry/node's NodeFetch integration never attaches. The node control run on the same `build/` emitted `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:41337/__rec/from-sveltekit` and propagated both headers.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: A module-scope `mysql2/promise` pool queried from `/api/db` produced no db span on bun. mysql2 3.24.3 publishes its own `mysql2:query`/`execute`/`connect` tracing channels and Sentry's `Mysql2` integration subscribes to them, but on bun `tracingChannel('mysql2:query').start.hasSubscribers` is `false` (node: `true`), so nothing is ever recorded. Instrumentation path: no Bun plugin build was used or needed — SvelteKit's own Vite/rolldown build is the bundle, and the Sentry Vite plugin did inject into it (`globalThis.__SENTRY_ORCHESTRION_INJECT__ = orchestrionModuleInjected("mysql2", mysql2Integration)` sits in the emitted route chunk). The failure is on the subscriber side at startup: `Sentry.init` logs `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` on bun, yet the acs binding the subscriber waits for IS present later (`acs.getTracingChannelBinding()` returns truthy at request time on both runtimes), so `waitForTracingChannelBinding`'s single 1 ms retry window is simply missed on bun.

Scope: probed the develop SDK only (worktree 6f2da7483d, version 10.67.0). 10.73.0 was never installed.

What bun costs you, precisely: everything that rides on SvelteKit's own request path works (errors, route names, isolation, incoming trace, SSR trace meta tags, logs, static and stream lifecycles both). Everything that rides on Node diagnostics-channel instrumentation is silently dead (outgoing fetch spans + propagation headers, mysql2 db spans, and by extension every other library integration in @sentry/node). The failure is silent unless `debug: true` is on, where it shows as one line: "No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping." I verified the same `build/` directory run under node emits the missing spans, so the SvelteKit build and the Vite-plugin injection are not the problem — the runtime is.

Refinement on the root cause, since it is not the obvious one: the injected orchestrion marker IS present in the emitted route chunk, bun DOES implement `diagnostics_channel.tracingChannel` correctly (verified standalone in `dctest.mjs`: `start.hasSubscribers` flips to `true` on subscribe, `traceCallback`/`tracePromise` are functions), and the async-context binding the subscriber waits for IS available on bun at request time (`/api/acs` returns `binding: true` on both runtimes). What never happens on bun is the subscribe itself. `waitForTracingChannelBinding` (packages/core/src/asyncContext/tracing-channel-binding.ts:9) checks the binding once, then retries exactly once after `setTimeout(..., 1)` and gives up. On bun the acs is evidently installed later than that window. A larger/looping retry, or re-checking on the first client request, would likely light up the whole library-instrumentation surface on bun for every @sentry/node-based framework SDK, not just SvelteKit. Worth a targeted experiment before anyone writes a "SvelteKit on bun" docs page.

Two findings that are NOT bun-specific but showed up here and reproduce on node with the identical build:
- With `experimental.tracing.server: true` but `Sentry.init()` still called from `hooks.server.ts` (the pre-instrumentation.server wiring), the SDK emits zero transaction/span envelopes. Errors still flow. Silent, and an easy trap for anyone following an older guide.
- With kit tracing on, a route that 500s yields `status: "ok"` on the `http.server` span. `instrumentHandle` only calls `setHttpStatus` on the span it created itself; when `event.tracing.enabled` it reuses kit's root span and passes no span, so the status is never set (packages/sveltekit/src/server-common/handle.ts, `resolveWithSentry`).

Also of note: `request.url` on captured events reads `https://127.0.0.1:41338/...` for a plain-HTTP adapter-node server on both runtimes.

notes:
Two findings worth filing.

(a) BUILD BREAK, Sentry-caused: with the exact docs config, `vite build` dies in SvelteKit's postbuild `analyse` step the moment a route imports `mysql`. The orchestrion/server-runtime-injection transform run by `sentrySvelteKit()` rewrites the bundled CJS driver and emits `import require$$0 from "@sentry/core"` into the SSR chunk; `@sentry/core` is ESM-only and left external by SvelteKit's SSR externalization, so Node throws `does not provide an export named 'default'`. Control proves it is Sentry's: the identical app builds cleanly with only `sentrySvelteKit()` removed. `ssr: { noExternal: ['@sentry/core','@sentry/conventions','@opentelemetry/api'] }` fixes it (the db-mysql chunk then weighs 2.36 MB). The in-repo e2e app dev-packages/e2e-tests/test-applications/sveltekit-cloudflare-pages has the same mysql route and does NOT carry this workaround, so it is worth checking whether that app's pinned @sveltejs/kit 2.69.1 / pnpm layout hides the same defect.

(b) SEGMENT NAME never gets the route. `svelteKitSpansIntegration` sets the parameterized name and `http.route` on a CHILD span, while the segment stays the Cloudflare request span (`GET /users/42` source url under static, bare `GET` under stream). Both lifecycles were checked. On the Node SvelteKit SDK the SvelteKit span IS the root, so this is Cloudflare-specific and means transaction grouping in the product is by URL, not by route.

- `@sentry/sveltekit@10.67.0` cannot be installed from $REPRO/_toolbox/pack alone: its `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` dependency is neither in $REPRO/_toolbox/pack nor published (npm latest 10.73.0). It has to be packed from the worktree. Worth adding to $REPRO/_toolbox/pack for other framework cells.
- The Worker reaches the host sink at `127.0.0.1:41317` fine; `tunnel` in `initCloudflareSentryHandle` works.
- mysql connections must be created INSIDE the handler on workerd (module-scope I/O is forbidden), the inverse of the Bun K11 rule, and spans still attach correctly.
- npm 11 skipped the workerd/esbuild postinstall scripts (`npm warn allow-scripts`); the prebuilt binaries were present anyway and wrangler dev started fine, so no approval was needed.
- Processes killed (sink 49140, recorder 49142, wrangler 59970); app/node_modules removed, directory down to 6.6 MB.

notes:
Headline: SvelteKit + @sentry/sveltekit runs on Deno better than expected. The server side is the full @sentry/node SDK with OpenTelemetry, and it boots and works under Deno with no import hook, no --import flag, and no @sentry/deno involvement — Sentry.init in hooks.server.js is sufficient. Errors, route names with source "route", isolation across concurrent requests, incoming trace continuation and logs all work. Two things are broken and one docs bug.

1) Broken, and this is the serious one: with the SDK loaded, importing mysql2 crashes the app on Deno. `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` registers `Module.registerHooks()`; its code transformer throws on mysql2 ("TypeError: transform is not a function"), and after that mysql2's `require('../package.json')` fails with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'` because the hooked CJS loader compiles JSON as JavaScript. The same connection and query succeed on Deno 2.9.0 when Sentry is absent. So this is not just "no db spans", the SDK takes a working route down. It is the same failure class as the known Deno finding K3 (denoland/deno#36240, JSON require under a module hook), but reached through the Node SDK's Module.registerHooks path rather than `@sentry/deno/import`, which means it also hits any Node-SDK-on-Deno deployment, not just apps that opted into the Deno hook. Any CJS dependency that does `require('*.json')` is affected.

2) Broken: global fetch gets no http.client span and no sentry-trace/baggage headers. Deno emits no undici diagnostics-channel events. The node:http contrast probe in the same handler works fully (span plus both headers), which pins the cause to the fetch instrumentation channel rather than to tracing or propagation. Consequence for a SvelteKit user: SvelteKit's idiomatic `event.fetch` / `fetch` calls in load functions and endpoints produce no distributed trace on Deno.

3) Develop API change vs docs: `sentrySvelteKit` is only exported from `@sentry/sveltekit/vite` on develop. Importing it from `@sentry/sveltekit` (what the v10 docs show) fails the Vite config load with "does not provide an export named 'sentrySvelteKit'". Whatever docs page covers SvelteKit needs updating for v11.

Local packaging artifacts, not user-facing bugs: (a) npm resolved @sentry/bundler-plugins and @sentry/cloudflare from the registry at the released 10.67.0, which then failed against develop's @sentry/core with "does not provide an export named 'ServerRuntimeClient'"; passing those two develop tarballs on the install line fixed it. (b) Vite inlines mysql2 and the SDK into the SSR bundle unless you set ssr.external / rollupOptions.external, which the SDK itself warns about at runtime.

Noise worth a docs or SDK note: on Deno the ContextLines integration spams "Failed to read file: ext:deno_node/async_hooks.ts ... ENOENT" and "Could not find line N in file ext:core/01_core.js" for every event, because Deno's internal frames use ext: URLs. Events still carry context lines for user frames (hasContextLine true).

Ports used and released: sink 52431, recorder 52432, app 52433. All processes killed; node_modules (138M) removed. One mid-run gotcha for other agents: another agent's Deno server held 127.0.0.1:41337 while mine bound 0.0.0.0:41337, so curl silently hit theirs (an Astro 404 page). Bind HOST=127.0.0.1 explicitly.

setup:
TanStack Start itself runs on bun without Sentry: `vite build` (nitro node-server preset) then `PORT=

bun .output/server/index.mjs` serves SSR pages and `server.handlers` API routes correctly. Wiring Sentry the way the docs page describes DOES NOT BUILD with npm-installed develop packages, so a docs page for this combination cannot be written as-is today. What the docs currently prescribe (manual-setup/index.mdx): install @sentry/tanstackstart-react; `instrument.server.mjs` with Sentry.init at the root; `src/server.ts` wrapping the server entry with `wrapFetchWithSentry`; `src/start.ts` adding `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` / `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware`; `sentryTanstackStart()` in vite.config.ts; run with `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`. On bun the run command becomes `bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, and that part works (Sentry.init runs, `getClient()` is truthy). Three build blockers hit before anything ran: 1. Any `import ... from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'` inside the server module graph (src/server.ts, src/start.ts, src/router.tsx, or any route file) makes `vite build` fail in the nitro environment with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'getVariableForExportName')`. Patching rollup to log showed the null re-export target is `__exports` imported by `@sentry/server-runtime-injection/build/esm/vendored/source-map/lib/base64.js` (that package's ESM build re-exports through `_virtual/*.js` namespace shims that rollup cannot resolve once the package is partially externalized by nitro's dep tracing). 2. Adding `sentryTanstackStart()` to vite.config.ts together with a `mysql` import fails the SSR build earlier: `"default" is not exported by "node_modules/@sentry/conventions/dist/attributes.mjs"` — the build-time diagnostics-channel injection emits a CJS `require('@sentry/conventions/attributes')` that rollup resolves to the .mjs. 3. Tarball packaging friction (not an SDK bug for real users): the registry `@sentry/bundler-plugins@10.67.0` imports `ServerRuntimeClient` from `@sentry/core`, which develop removed, and `@sentry/browser` 10.67.0 (develop) pulls registry `@sentry/feedback` / `@sentry/replay` / `@sentry/replay-canvas` / `@sentry/browser-utils` which break the client build. Fixed by packing feedback/replay-internal/replay-canvas/browser-utils from the worktree and nesting the registry @sentry/core under @sentry/bundler-plugins. Working setup actually probed (docs would have to describe this, or the build bugs must be fixed): - `npm install @tanstack/react-start@1.168.35 @tanstack/react-router@1.170.18 react react-dom nitro@3.0.260610-beta mysql vite@7.3.2 @vitejs/plugin-react-swc vite-tsconfig-paths` plus the Sentry tarballs. - `vite.config.ts`: `tsConfigPaths(), tanstackStart(), nitro(), viteReact()` — WITHOUT `sentryTanstackStart()`. - `instrument.server.mjs` at the app root: `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'; Sentry.init({ dsn, tunnel, tracesSampleRate: 1, traceLifecycle }); globalThis.__PROBE_SENTRY__ = Sentry;` - `src/probe/sentry.ts` shim re-exporting `wrapFetchWithSentry`, `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware`, `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware`, `setTag`, `captureException`, `captureMessage`, `logger` off `globalThis.__PROBE_SENTRY__`, so no `@sentry/*` specifier ever enters the rollup graph. `src/server.ts` and `src/start.ts` import from that shim instead of the package. - Build: `npx vite build`. Run: `PORT=41500 bun --preload ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`.

The single documented run command is `manual-setup/index.mdx:372` `"start": "node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs"`, and `manual-setup/index.mdx:383` frames the alternative as "when you can't configure Node.js CLI flags". Conversely `~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/bun/` never mentions TanStack. `manual-setup/index.mdx:17` does flag the whole SDK as beta ("compatible with TanStack Start 1.0 RC and is currently in beta").
notes:
Bottom line: TanStack Start runs on bun, and @sentry/tanstackstart-react initializes on bun, but only errors and logs work. Everything that depends on per-request async context or on module patching — server transactions/route names, isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing fetch headers and spans, db spans — is broken, and the failures are all one root cause: on bun there is no way to install the diagnostics-channel injection hooks or patch node:http, so @sentry/node's server span never exists and the isolation scope is never forked. The SDK says both out loud with debug:true ("No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping." and "No diagnostics-channel injection detected."), which is honest but it does not warn that request isolation is gone; silently sharing one process-global isolation scope and one process-global trace id across concurrent requests is the most dangerous finding here, because it leaks tags (and would leak user data) between users' requests without any error.

Separately, the docs wiring does not even build with develop packages installed via npm. A single `import { wrapFetchWithSentry } from '@sentry/tanstackstart-react'` in the server module graph kills `vite build`'s nitro pass with a rollup null-module crash traced to `@sentry/server-runtime-injection`'s vendored source-map ESM (`_virtual/*.js` `__exports` re-export shims). That is runtime-independent — it would hit a Node user on npm just the same — so it deserves checking against the repo's pnpm-based e2e app, which builds the identical wiring fine; the difference is almost certainly npm hoisting versus pnpm symlinks changing what nitro's dep tracing externalizes. Adding `sentryTanstackStart()` on top, with a `mysql` import present, fails earlier and differently: the build-time channel injection emits `require('@sentry/conventions/attributes')` inside a CJS module and rollup resolves that specifier to `attributes.mjs`, which has no default export.

I worked around both by keeping every `@sentry/*` specifier out of the bundle: `instrument.server.mjs` is `--preload`ed by bun and stashes the namespace on `globalThis`, and `src/probe/sentry.ts` re-exports from there. That is not a shape any docs page should recommend, but it let the seven capabilities be measured rather than reported as not-run.

One more thing worth chasing outside this cell: the same build, on Node v26.5.0, is fine with `node .output/server/index.mjs` and completely broken with `node --import ./instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs` — every API route answers 200 with a two-byte `{}` body and nothing reaches the sink. That looks like @sentry/node's http instrumentation colliding with nitro/srvx on Node 26, and it means the documented TanStack Start start command may be broken on current Node independently of bun.

Constraints on the numbers: single machine, one bun version (1.4.0), one nitro beta (I also tried 3.0.260903-beta with the same rollup crash), one TanStack Start version. The db-span verdict is "no span observed" rather than "instrumentation proven impossible" — the injection path could not be tested at all because the build that would produce it fails.

framework: TanStack Start (React) v1.136 with @tanstack/react-start file-based routing
runtime: Cloudflare Workers (workerd 2026-09-03 via wrangler 4.129.0 local dev, nodejs_compat, compatibility_date 2026-05-01)

capabilities.name: errors
capabilities.detail: An Error thrown from a `createFileRoute('/users/$id').server.handlers.GET` handler reaches Sentry as an unhandled exception with mechanism `auto.middleware.tanstackstart.request` (the `sentryGlobalRequestMiddleware` catch/rethrow), `handled: false`, and `transaction: "GET /users/$id"`. The framework does not swallow it: the request still returns HTTP 500 and the accompanying transaction has `status: internal_error`. Same result in both static and stream lifecycle. Stack frames have no `context_line` because I disabled sourcemaps in the build.

capabilities.name: route names
capabilities.detail: static lifecycle: `transaction: "GET /users/$id"`, `source: "route"`, `http.route: "/users/$id"`. stream lifecycle: span `http.server GET /users/$id` with `sentry.segment.name.source = route`. This depends entirely on `sentryTanstackStart()` being in vite.config.ts - its `makeRoutePatternPlugin` defines `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__`, which `wrapFetchWithSentry` reads. With the plugin removed (i.e. the exact config the docs page shows) the same request produced `"GET /users/123"` with `source: "url"` and no `http.route`.

capabilities.name: isolation
capabilities.detail: Three concurrent GETs to /iso/alpha, /iso/bravo, /iso/charlie, each calling Sentry.setTag('probe_tag', <tag>), sleeping 120ms, then captureException. Each of the three events carried exactly its own tag and nothing else, and each event's trace_id matched its own transaction's trace_id (alpha=0d48d885…, bravo=bfadcc15…, charlie=3ca5fa81…). No cross-talk. static lifecycle.

capabilities.name: incoming trace
capabilities.detail: GET /users/77 with `sentry-trace: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111-1122334455667788-1` and a matching baggage header produced a transaction with `trace_id: aaaabbbbccccddddeeeeffff00001111` and `parent_span_id: 1122334455667788`, still named `GET /users/$id` with `source: route`. static lifecycle.

capabilities.name: outgoing fetch
capabilities.detail: A `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:33518/rec')` from inside a route handler produced an `http.client GET http://127.0.0.1:33518/rec` child span in the transaction (stream lifecycle names it `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`, the new low-cardinality name), and the recorder saw both `sentry-trace: 1618d771012e44be8077b306c7408659-b87a74f6c91b675a-1` and a full baggage header including `sentry-transaction=GET%20%2Fapi%2Fprobe-fetch`. Trace id matches the server transaction.

capabilities.name: db spans
capabilities.detail: Module-scope `mysql.createPool({host:'127.0.0.1',port:3307,...})` plus `pool.query('SELECT id, name FROM users')` inside the handler returned real rows from MariaDB and produced a `db SELECT id, name FROM users` child span (stream lifecycle: `db SELECT users`). Instrumentation path: the Cloudflare-side Vite plugin chain, specifically `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` inside `sentryTanstackStart()` - NOT `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin`, which is not used at all in a TanStack Start app. It was needed: the bundle grew from 191kB to 2.6MB (the plugin's `ssr.noExternal` force-bundles mysql) and contains the injected channels `orchestrion:mysql:query`, `orchestrion:mysql2:query`, `orchestrion:mysql2:execute`. With `sentryTanstackStart()` removed the identical request produced a transaction with `spans: []`. Note the plugin is production-only (`process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` returns early), so `vite dev` gets no db spans.

capabilities.name: logs
capabilities.detail: `Sentry.logger.info('tanstack cf probe log', { where: 'route-handler' })` from a route handler arrived as a `log` envelope item `info: tanstack cf probe log` carrying the same trace_id (502d6782cfa04424b727e0df8a0e4b77) as the enclosing `GET /api/probe-log` transaction. No `enableLogs` option needed on develop. Flushed within the 8s wait. static lifecycle.

A dedicated page exists and is broadly correct: ~/dev/sentry-docs/docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx (290 lines, "TanStack Start on Cloudflare", linked from guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:23). Gap: the page never tells the user to add `sentryTanstackStart()` from `@sentry/tanstackstart-react/vite` to vite.config.ts. Line 10 is the ONLY occurrence of the string "vite" in the whole file, and it is prose ("using the `@cloudflare/vite-plugin`"); there is no vite.config.ts snippet anywhere. `grep -n "sentryTanstackStart\|vite.config" docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/tanstack-start.mdx` returns nothing. Following the page literally therefore yields url-source transaction names (`GET /users/123`) and zero db/library spans, which I confirmed with the control run above. The plugin lives one guide over, at docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/features/sentryTanstackStart.mdx, with no cross-link from the Cloudflare page.

Second, unrelated mention: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx:391 says "This setup doesn't work for Cloudflare deployments." about the Node `--import`-less variant. That is accurate but reads as a dead end - it does not point at the Cloudflare guide's working path.
notes:
- TanStack Start on Workers is fully viable and every probed capability passed. This is the strongest Cloudflare framework result I would expect: parametrized route names, working isolation across concurrent requests, trace continuation, client-span headers, db spans and logs all work with one build config.
- Every result above came from `traceLifecycle: 'static'` except the block explicitly labelled stream; I re-ran errors, route names, outgoing fetch and db spans under `'stream'` too and all four held (stream additionally gave the new low-cardinality names `db SELECT users` and `http.client GET 127.0.0.1`).
- The single load-bearing thing the docs omit is `sentryTanstackStart()` in vite.config.ts. It is what defines `__SENTRY_ROUTE_PATTERNS__` (read by `wrapFetchWithSentry` -> `updateSpanWithRouteParametrization`) and what runs `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` for db/library instrumentation. Note also that `sentryOrchestrionPlugin` is skipped when `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'`, so `vite dev` never produces db spans on this stack - only `vite build` + `wrangler dev` does.
- `sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite` is NOT part of this setup and should not be added; the TanStack Start plugin chain plus explicit `withSentry` in src/server.ts covers it.
- `@sentry/tanstackstart-react`'s server entry does `export * from '@sentry/node'`, which sounds fatal on workerd but is not: the package's `workerd`/`worker` export conditions map to index.server, and the Cloudflare Vite plugin tree-shakes away everything except the helpers actually imported (`wrapFetchWithSentry`, the two middlewares). Worth knowing because it looks like a blocker on inspection.
- Not probed: server functions (`createServerFn`) - the app has the routes from the e2e scaffold but I focused the seven listed capabilities on route handlers. The `sentryGlobalFunctionMiddleware` renames those spans to `GET /_serverFn/<name>` per src/server/globalMiddleware.ts.
- Environment friction, not SDK: ports 41337/41338 and 52731 were already held by other agents' processes on this machine; I moved to 33517/33518/33519. Also, backgrounding a server with `&` inside a plain Bash call makes the call hang until the 2-minute timeout and then kills the child - servers must be started with `run_in_background`.
- Cleanup done: all three background processes stopped, ports 33517/33518/33519 verified free, `node_modules` (375M) removed. The MariaDB container was pre-existing and left untouched.

The TanStack Start guide is Node-only by construction: docs/platforms/javascript/guides/tanstackstart-react/manual-setup/index.mdx:9 tags it `server-node`, :300 heads the recommended section "With `--import` Flag (e.g. Node.js Server)", and :372 gives the start script `node --import ./.output/server/instrument.server.mjs .output/server/index.mjs`, a flag Deno does not have. The only alternative the page offers (:383-389, "when you can't configure Node.js CLI flags") explicitly instruments native Node APIs only. So a user on Deno has no documented init placement; the two-line `deno-entry.mjs` above is what a Deno page would have to show.
notes:
- TanStack Start's nitro node output runs on Deno 2.9 unmodified: SSR page routes, file-based API routes, `$id` params and thrown-error 500s all behave the same as on node v26.5.0. Deno reports itself as `runtime: {name: "node", version: "v26.3.0"}` in Sentry events.
- @sentry/node's runtime instrumentation works on Deno through `Module.registerHooks()` (the SDK logs "Registered diagnostics-channel injection via Module.registerHooks()"), and the eager Bun/Deno channel subscriptions fire. This is why the mysql span appears without any @sentry/deno import hook.
- Biggest finding, and it is NOT Deno-specific: with this dependency set (npm-installed 10.67.0 tarballs + nitro 3.0.260903-beta + vite 7.3.2 + rollup 4.63.1) `vite build` of the standard tanstackstart-react app fails. Nitro's SSR rollup pass resolves @sentry/* to their CJS builds while resolving what those files `require()` to ESM, so rollup-plugin-commonjs emits `import require$$0 from "@sentry/conventions/attributes"` / `"@sentry/core"` against ESM files with no default export. Contributing factor: `@sentry/tanstackstart-react`'s `exports["."]` map has only `workerd`/`worker`/`browser`/`node` conditions and no `default`, so a bundler environment that matches none of them falls back to the CJS `main`. Nitro also warns `vite@7.3.2 is installed but the vite builder requires ^8`.
